Kyberheart

Your hub for Kyberheart, the Star Wars roleplaying game built on Daggerheart: the full rules, character creation and playable sheets, and tools for running the table.

Chapter 1

Introduction

Introduction

Welcome to KYBERHEART, a Star Wars hack of the DAGGERHEART roleplaying game: a collaborative tabletop game of blaster fights, starship chases, and heroes who stand against the darkness of a galaxy far, far away.

What Is This?

This is the Kyberheart SRD (System Reference Document). It collects every Kyberheart rule, class, card, ancestry, community, item, starship, adversary, and environment in one place, organized like the official Daggerheart SRD for quick reference.

Kyberheart is built on the Daggerheart SRD 1.0 using the Daggerheart Homebrew Kit v1.0. Wherever this document doesn't change a rule, the Daggerheart SRD's rule applies unchanged. Keep both documents at the table.

The Basics

Kyberheart plays exactly like Daggerheart:

  • Duality Dice: When your character attempts something risky, roll two d12s, the Hope Die and the Fear Die, and add a trait. Meet or beat the Difficulty to succeed. Whichever die rolled higher decides whether you roll with Hope or with Fear.

  • Hope and Fear: Rolling with Hope gives you a Hope to fuel your features. Rolling with Fear gives the GM a Fear to fuel theirs.

  • The spotlight: There's no initiative. The spotlight moves to whoever the story turns to, and swings to the GM when a player fails or rolls with Fear.

  • Damage: Damage is compared to your Major and Severe thresholds to decide how many Hit Points you mark. Armor Slots reduce its severity.

The Golden Rule

Daggerheart SRD rule, unchanged in Kyberheart.

The most important rule of Kyberheart is to make the game your own. The rules included in this SRD are designed to help you enjoy the experience at the table, but everyone has a different approach to interpreting rules and telling stories. The rules should never get in the way of the story you want to tell, the characters you want to play, or the adventures you want to have. As long as your group agrees, everything can be adjusted to fit your play style. If there’s a rule you’d rather ignore or modify, feel free to implement any change with your table’s consent.

Rulings Over Rules

While playing Kyberheart, the GM and players should always prioritize rulings over rules. This SRD offers answers for many questions your table may have about the game, but it won’t answer all of them. When you’re in doubt about how a rule applies, the GM should make a ruling that aligns with the narrative.

For example, a grappling line lets you pull a target close to you. If you try to use it to pull an entire Star Destroyer, the weapon text doesn’t forbid you from doing that—but it doesn’t make sense within the narrative. Instead, the GM might rule that you pull a few bricks out, or pull yourself toward the wall instead.

Similarly, if your character does something that would logically result in immediate death—such as diving into an active volcano without protection—you might not get to make one of Kyberheart’s death moves, which normally give you control of your character’s fate in their final moments. This kind of consequence should be made clear before the action is completed, and it should always follow the logic of the world. As a narrative-focused game, Kyberheart is not a place where technical, out-of-context interpretations of the rules are encouraged. Everything should flow back to the fiction, and the GM has the authority and responsibility to make rulings about how rules are applied to underscore that fiction.

Chapter 2

Character Creation

Character Creation

You can fill in your character's name, pronouns, and description at any point during character creation.

Step 1: Choose a Class and Subclass

Classes are role-based archetypes that determine which class features and class cards your character can access. Kyberheart has ten classes: Force Adept, Scout, Scoundrel, Guardian, Pilot, Bounty Hunter, Soldier, Technician, Consular, and Operative.

  • Choose a class and record its starting Evasion, Hit Points, Hope Feature, and class features.

  • Choose one of the class's two subclasses and take its foundation features.

Step 2: Choose Your Heritage

Your heritage combines your ancestry and your community.

  • Ancestry is your species. It grants two ancestry features. Choose from: Chiss, Droid, Duros, Ewok, Gungan, Human, Jawa, Mirialan, Mon Calamari, Rodian, Sullustan, Togruta, Trandoshan, Twi'lek, Wookiee, and Zabrak. To create a Mixed Ancestry, take the first feature of one ancestry and the second feature of another.

  • Community is the culture or way of life that raised you. It grants one community feature. Choose from: Jedi Order, Sith Acolytes, Mandalorian Covert, Batch, Rebel Cell, Imperial Academy, City-World, Canopy Clans, Dune Sea, Spacer, Orbital Shipyards, Syndicate, Spynet, and Hunting Lodge.

Step 3: Assign Character Traits

Your character has six traits: Agility (sprint, leap, maneuver), Strength (lift, smash, grapple), Finesse (control, hide, tinker), Instinct (perceive, sense, navigate), Presence (charm, perform, deceive), and Knowledge (recall, analyze, comprehend). Assign the modifiers +2, +1, +1, +0, +0, and −1 to your traits in any order. Each class lists suggested traits.

Step 4: Record Additional Character Information

  • You start at level 1.

  • Record your class's starting Evasion and Hit Points.

  • Every PC starts with 6 Stress slots and 2 Hope.

Step 5: Choose Your Starting Equipment

  • Weapons: Choose from the Tier 1 weapon tables: a two-handed primary weapon, or a one-handed primary weapon and a one-handed secondary weapon. Your Proficiency starts at 1.

  • Armor: Choose one set of Tier 1 armor. Add your level to its base thresholds to find your damage thresholds.

  • Inventory: A glow rod, 50 feet of synthrope, basic supplies, a handful of credits, and either a Bacta Patch (clear 1d4 Hit Points) or a Stamina Stim (clear 1d4 Stress).

  • Class items: Choose one of your class's two class items.

Each class lists suggested starting gear.

Step 6: Create Your Background

Answer your class's background questions, or write your own history.

Step 7: Create Your Experiences

An Experience is a word or phrase that sums up a set of skills, personality traits, or aptitudes your character has gained. When you make a move, you can spend a Hope to add a relevant Experience's modifier to the action roll.

  • You start with two Experiences, each at +2.

  • You gain a new Experience at +2 at levels 2, 5, and 8.

  • An Experience can't be too broad (like Strong in the Force or Lucky) or grant a special ability or Force power (like Mind Tricks or Can't Be Hit). The Force comes from the Force Adept class, not Experiences, but anyone can know Force lore.

Example Experiences

Step 8: Choose Class Cards

Take two of your class's three level 1 cards from your class’s deck, on its class page. Cards in your loadout are active; you can have up to five in your loadout at a time, as with Daggerheart's domain cards.

Kyberheart also lets you trade a starting card for one from another class’s deck: see Cross-Training in Kyberheart Mechanics.

Step 9: Create Your Connections

Describe your characters to one another, then answer each other's connection questions to build the relationships between your PCs.

Chapter 3

Core Materials

Core Materials

Class Cards

In Daggerheart, classes draw cards from two shared domains. In Kyberheart, each class has its own deck of 21 class cards: three at level 1 and two at every level from 2 to 10. A deck replaces its class's domains everywhere the Daggerheart SRD mentions domain cards.

  • Starting cards: At level 1, take two of your class's three level 1 cards.

  • Loadout and vault: You can have up to five cards in your loadout. Cards beyond five go in your vault. Moving a card from your vault to your loadout costs its Recall Cost, as in the SRD.

  • Card types: Cards are Abilities, Spells, or Grimoires. Guardian and Soldier decks hold only Abilities, because those classes have no Spellcast trait.

  • Spells: Only Force Adept spells are the Force. For every other class, a Spell is a trained technique that uses the subclass's Spellcast trait.

  • Damage types: Only the Force deals magic damage. Every other card that deals damage deals physical damage.

  • Grimoires: Technician and Operative grimoires are kits that each hold several functions.

The full text of every card is in its class’s deck, on the class page.

Classes

Force AdeptEvasion 10 · HP 6Jedi, Sith, Force-sensitive mysticScoutEvasion 12 · HP 6Pathfinder, survivalist, sharpshooterScoundrelEvasion 11 · HP 6Smuggler, gambler, gunslingerGuardianEvasion 9 · HP 7Bodyguard, Royal Guard, frontline protectorPilotEvasion 11 · HP 6Ace pilot, starfighter jockey, getaway driverBounty HunterEvasion 10 · HP 6Bounty hunter, mercenary trackerSoldierEvasion 10 · HP 7Clone trooper, Rebel infantry, stormtrooperTechnicianEvasion 11 · HP 5Mechanic, slicer, droid specialistConsularEvasion 10 · HP 6Diplomat, senator, leaderOperativeEvasion 12 · HP 5Spy, assassin, infiltrator

Every subclass has foundation, specialization, and mastery features. You gain the foundation at level 1. The upgraded subclass advancement, available in Tiers 3 and 4, grants the specialization and then the mastery.

Ancestries

Your ancestry is your character's species. Each ancestry grants two ancestry features: the first describes what the species is, and the second describes what the species does. Ancestry features are physical or biological; culture belongs to communities.

  • Mixed Ancestry: Take the first feature of one ancestry and the second feature of another.

  • Advantage doesn't stack: If two sources give advantage on the same roll, you still roll one extra d6.

Chiss

Blue-skinned, red-eyed humanoids from Csilla in the Unknown Regions.

Red Eyes: Your vision edges into the infrared. Dim light never imposes disadvantage on your rolls, and you can see the heat of living creatures within Close range, even in darkness.

Pattern Recognition: Once per rest, after you watch an adversary act, you can ask the GM how it's likely to act next and how best to counter it.

Droid

Droid

Mechanical beings built to serve in countless roles, with varying degrees of artificial intelligence.

Purposeful Design: Decide who built you, for what purpose, and choose a chassis (Protocol, Astromech, Battle, or Labor; this is flavor only). At character creation, choose one of your Experiences that best aligns with this purpose and gain a permanent +1 bonus to it.

Self-Repair Protocols: You don't need to eat, sleep, or breathe. When you take a short rest, you can clear 1 additional Hit Point or Armor Slot of your choice. Ion weapons and EMPs are your weakness: when you take damage from one, mark an additional Stress.

Duros

Blue-green spacefarers from Duro, with large red eyes and long, lipless faces.

Steady in the Void: You have advantage on rolls to resist the effects of zero gravity, vertigo, and disorientation.

Born Navigator: You have advantage on rolls to plot a course, read star charts, or navigate hyperspace routes.

Ewok

Small, furry people from the forest moon of Endor, quick and hard to pin down.

Nimble Scrambler: You have advantage on Agility Rolls to climb or move through tight spaces.

Small Target: Gain a permanent +1 bonus to your Evasion at character creation.

Gungan

Amphibious people from Naboo, with long ears, powerful legs, and longer tongues.

Swift Swimmer: You can breathe and move naturally underwater, and you can hold your breath on land for a very long time.

Long Tongue: You can use your long tongue to grab onto things within Close range. Mark a Stress to use your tongue as a Finesse Close weapon that deals d12 physical damage using your Proficiency.

Human

The most widespread sentient species in the galaxy, found on nearly every settled world.

Hardy Physiology: You have advantage on rolls to resist hostile environments, such as extreme heat or cold, thin atmosphere, or heavy gravity.

Adaptability: When you fail a roll that used one of your Experiences, you can mark a Stress to reroll.

Jawa

Small, hooded scavengers from Tatooine, with glowing eyes beneath their robes.

Scent Speech: You can convey emotions and simple messages to other Jawas through scent, and you can recognize any creature you've met before by its smell.

Scurry: Once per rest, when an attack against you fails, you can move to any point within Close range without a roll.

Mirialan

Graceful near-humans from Mirial, known for remarkable flexibility and agility.

Acrobatic Grace: You have advantage on Agility Rolls to leap, tumble, or balance.

Contortion: When you would become Restrained, you can mark a Stress to twist free and avoid the condition.

Mon Calamari

Amphibious humanoids from Mon Cala, with high-domed heads and large, wide-set eyes.

Amphibious: You can breathe and move naturally underwater.

Wide-Set Eyes: Your eyes see nearly all the way around you. Once per rest, you can mark a Stress to force an adversary to reroll an attack against you or an ally within Very Close range.

Rodian

Reptilian humanoids from Rodia, with suction-cupped fingers and large eyes that see heat.

Suction Tips: You can climb vines, trees, walls, and other rough or slick surfaces, including overhead, without a roll. You have advantage on rolls to keep your hold, such as resisting being shaken loose, disarmed, or thrown.

Infrared Sight: You can see living creatures and warm objects in darkness within Far range, and darkness never imposes disadvantage on your rolls.

Sullustan

Large-eyed cave dwellers from Sullust, with big ears and a flawless sense of place.

Cave-Adapted Senses: Dim light never imposes disadvantage on your rolls, and you have advantage on Instinct Rolls that rely on hearing.

Spatial Memory: You remember every place you have been in precise detail. Once per rest, you can ask the GM to describe one detail of a location you have previously visited.

Togruta

Tall near-humans from Shili with colorful skin, hollow montrals, and white facial markings.

Montral Sense: Your montrals sense the space around you. You ignore disadvantage from darkness, concealment, or blindness against targets within Close range.

Camouflage: While you're Hidden or in dim light or darkness, you gain a +1 bonus to your Evasion.

Trandoshan

Large reptilian hunters from Trandosha, with clawed hands and bodies that heal and regrow.

Regeneration: When you take the Tend to Wounds downtime move on yourself, clear 1 additional Hit Point. Lost limbs regrow over time.

Rending Claws: Make a Strength Roll to rake a target within Melee range with your claws. On a success, they become temporarily Vulnerable.

Twi'lek

Near-humans from Ryloth, with two long, sensitive head-tails called lekku.

Sensitive Lekku: Your lekku pick up the slightest touch, vibration, and shift in the air. When you make a reaction roll, you can spend a Hope to gain advantage on it.

Lekku Language: Your lekku convey emotion and simple messages through subtle movement. You can silently communicate with allies within Close range who can see you, and you have advantage on Instinct Rolls to read the emotions of anyone whose body language you can observe.

Wookiee

Towering, fur-covered warriors from Kashyyyk, famous for their strength and long lives.

Mighty Frame: Gain an additional Hit Point slot at character creation.

Wookiee Charge: When you succeed on an Agility Roll to move from Far or Very Far range into Melee range with one or more targets, you can mark a Stress to deal 1d12 physical damage to all targets within Melee range.

Zabrak

Near-humans from Iridonia and Dathomir, with crowns of horns and two hearts.

Double Cardio: Gain an additional Stress slot at character creation.

Pain Tolerance: Once per rest, when you take damage, you can mark a Stress to reduce its severity by one threshold.

Communities

Your community is the culture, faction, or way of life that most shaped your character's upbringing. Each community grants one community feature and lists six adjectives to inspire your character's personality and attitude.

Following the Homebrew Kit, community features come from cultural practice and shared knowledge, not biology or Force powers. Most grant advantage in specific situations. A useful test is the Kit's sentence: "I'm from a Rebel Cell, so of course I know how to set an ambush."

A community describes an upbringing, not a class. A Jedi Order community can belong to a Force Adept or to someone raised in a temple's service corps, and a Mandalorian Covert can raise a Soldier, a Bounty Hunter, or a Pilot.

GroupCommunities
Force traditionsJedi Order, Sith Acolytes
FactionsMandalorian Covert, Batch, Rebel Cell, Imperial Academy
Worlds and ways of lifeCity-World, Canopy Clans, Dune Sea, Spacer, Orbital Shipyards
Shadows and tradesSyndicate, Spynet, Hunting Lodge

Jedi Order

Being part of the Jedi Order means you were raised within one of its temples or outposts, whether the great Temple on Coruscant, a frontier enclave, or a hidden refuge after the Order's fall. Life there revolved around discipline, meditation, study in the archives, and service to others. Younglings learned to set aside fear and attachment, to defend rather than attack, and to seek peaceful solutions first. Not everyone raised in an enclave becomes a Knight: many serve in the archives, the healing halls, or the agricultural and exploration corps. Since the Order's fall, those raised in its halls often carry its lessons in secret.

Members of the Jedi Order are often calm, compassionate, disciplined, earnest, patient, and reserved.

The Code: Record three tenets of the Jedi Code or lessons your teachers instilled in you. Once per rest, when you describe how you're embodying one of these principles through your current action, you can roll a d20 as your Hope Die.

Sith Acolytes

Being part of the Sith Acolytes means you grew up among those who revere the dark side: a cult guarding Sith relics, Inquisitorius trainees, or devotees like the Acolytes of the Beyond. Your upbringing prized strength, ambition, and the hunger to take what others would deny you. You learned that secrets are power, that ancient sites still whisper, and that loyalty lasts only as long as it's useful. Some acolytes never touch the Force at all, serving instead as scholars, guardians, or zealots of a dead empire.

Sith Acolytes are often ambitious, cunning, driven, intense, proud, and secretive.

Forbidden Lore: You have advantage on rolls to recall Sith history, decipher ancient texts and artifacts, or recognize the influence of the dark side.

Mandalorian Covert

Being part of a Mandalorian Covert means you were raised in a hidden enclave of Mandalorian warriors, by blood or as a foundling taken in and sworn to the Creed. Coverts live apart and guard their ways fiercely. Children learn to fight, hunt, and maintain their armor and weapons from the moment they can lift them, and the clan's Armorer forges beskar into each warrior's legacy. Some coverts never remove their helmets before others; some live openly on Mandalore. All of them prize loyalty to clan and the strength to protect it.

Mandalorians are often devoted, fierce, guarded, honorable, resourceful, and stoic.

This Is the Way: You have advantage on rolls to size up a fighter or a battlefield, care for armor and weapons, or follow a target's trail.

Batch

Being part of a Batch means you were grown and trained alongside identical brothers in the cloning facilities of Kamino, or raised in a similarly regimented military program. From your first days, you drilled, studied tactics, and learned to function as one part of a unit. Your batchmates were your only family, and you know the cost of following orders as well as anyone. Many who left the program still check corners, count exits, and stand at attention without meaning to.

Batch members are often dutiful, efficient, loyal, pragmatic, steadfast, and weary.

Flash-Trained: You have advantage on rolls to recall military procedure, identify military hardware and tactics, or coordinate with soldiers who share your training.

Rebel Cell

Being part of a Rebel Cell means you grew up in the resistance: a small, isolated group fighting a much greater power from the shadows. Cells survived by secrecy and nerve, knowing only enough about other cells to work with them. You learned to strike and vanish, to make do with salvaged weapons, and to look like an ordinary civilian when the patrols came through. Above all, you learned that hope is worth fighting for.

Rebels are often defiant, hopeful, idealistic, resourceful, scrappy, and wary.

Guerrilla: You have advantage on rolls to set ambushes, sabotage equipment, or blend in with civilians.

Imperial Academy

Being part of an Imperial Academy means you were shaped by the officer schools and training programs of the Empire, or of another great galactic military. Every hour followed a schedule, every rank mattered, and every failure was recorded. You learned the regulations by heart, how to command and how to obey, and how to make a bureaucracy bend. Some graduates still believe in the order they were taught; others defected the moment they saw what it was for.

Imperials are often ambitious, disciplined, exacting, orderly, proud, and ruthless.

Chain of Command: You have advantage on rolls to recall regulations and protocol, read rank and authority, or bluff or bully your way past bureaucracy.

City-World

Being from a City-World means you grew up on a city-planet like Coruscant, where buildings cover every continent and the ground level hasn't seen sunlight in centuries. You learned to read traffic lanes, turbolift maps, and the shifting moods of a billion strangers. Some city-world dwellers live in spires above the clouds; others never leave the lower levels. Either way, you know that anything can be found in the city if you know who to ask.

City-dwellers are often cosmopolitan, jaded, quick, savvy, streetwise, and tireless.

Crowd-Born: You have advantage on rolls to navigate a city, lose a pursuer in a crowd, or find a specific person, business, or service.

Canopy Clans

Being part of the Canopy Clans means you grew up among the treetop villages of a forest world, like the Ewok settlements of Endor or the wroshyr-tree cities of Kashyyyk. Your people build high above the forest floor and defend their homes with cunning rather than heavy weapons. Children learn to climb before they can run, and every clan member knows how to turn vines, logs, and stones into deadly traps against invaders.

Canopy Clan members are often clever, fierce, loyal, nurturing, playful, and territorial.

Snares and Slings: Once per rest, you can rig a simple trap from natural materials. The first adversary to move through it must succeed on a Reaction Roll (13) or become Restrained until it breaks free.

Dune Sea

Being part of the Dune Sea means you grew up on a desert world like Tatooine, Jakku, or Jedha, where water is wealth and the suns show no mercy. Moisture farmers, scavengers, traders, and nomads all learn the same lessons: read the wind, ration every drop, and pick wrecks clean before someone else does. Desert folk are slow to trust and quick to bargain, and they know exactly how far it is to the next settlement.

Dune Sea folk are often hardy, independent, patient, resourceful, stubborn, and tight-lipped.

Desert-Wise: You have advantage on rolls to survive and navigate wastelands, or to scavenge usable parts and supplies from wrecks.

Spacer

Being a Spacer means you were raised aboard starships and space stations, rarely setting foot on a planet for long. Home was a freighter crew, a mining platform, or a trade convoy jumping from port to port. You grew up knowing every hatch and crawlspace aboard, which spaceport officials could be bribed, and which superstitions kept a ship lucky. Planets feel too big and too still.

Spacers are often adaptable, free-spirited, practical, restless, superstitious, and tight-knit.

Ship-Raised: You have advantage on rolls to find your way around starships and space stations, find hidden compartments, or book passage off-world.

Orbital Shipyards

Being part of the Orbital Shipyards means you grew up among the great starship builders of worlds like Kuat, Mon Cala, and Corellia. You were raised among drydocks, design studios, and test flights, where engineers argued over hull plating at dinner and every child could name a ship's class from its silhouette. Shipyard folk understand that every vessel and every plan has a flaw, if you know where to look.

Shipyard folk are often inventive, methodical, meticulous, proud, technical, and visionary.

Shipwright's Mind: You have advantage on rolls to study a starship or a battle plan and spot weaknesses, traps, or ambushes in it.

Syndicate

Being part of a Syndicate means you grew up in the galaxy's underworld, among the Hutt cartels, Black Sun, the Pyke Syndicate, Crimson Dawn, or smaller crews that answer to them. Spice runs, protection rackets, and smuggling routes were the family business. Syndicate members can be anyone from a crime lord's heir to a street-level runner, but all of them live by codes that are enforced swiftly and without mercy.

Syndicate members are often calculating, charming, cutthroat, opportunistic, shrewd, and tenacious.

Underworld Ties: You have advantage on rolls to negotiate with criminals, find a black market, or fence stolen goods.

Spynet

Being part of a Spynet means you were raised among information brokers, in one of the galaxy's spy rings where secrets are currency and everyone watches everyone else. You learned to listen more than you speak, to trade one rumor for two, and to never reveal your sources. Spynet members serve whoever pays best, or whichever cause they quietly believe in.

Spynet members are often curious, discreet, observant, paranoid, persuasive, and scheming.

Rumor Mill: When you arrive in a settlement or meet a faction, you can spend a Hope to ask the GM one question about its rumors, secrets, or hidden powers. The GM answers honestly.

Hunting Lodge

Being part of a Hunting Lodge means you were raised in a culture that measures worth by the hunt, like Trandoshan clans tallying points for the Scorekeeper, Rodian hunting traditions, or big-game guides on wild worlds. You learned patience, tracking, and the habits of every kind of prey, including sentient ones. Lodge members respect a worthy quarry and despise a sloppy kill.

Hunters are often competitive, patient, predatory, proud, relentless, and watchful.

Born Hunter: You have advantage on rolls to track or stalk prey.

class portrait

Force Adept

Force Adept

Force Adepts feel the Force flowing through every living thing and bend it to their will, as Jedi, Sith, or something in between.

Starting Evasion
10
Starting Hit Points
6
Class Items
A kyber crystal that once belonged to someone else, or a holocron you can't open

Force Adept's Hope Feature

The Force Is With Me: Spend 3 Hope after you make an action roll to reroll your Hope Die. You must use the new result.

Class Features

Force Sense: Spend a Hope to sense living beings and strong disturbances in the Force within Far range. The GM tells you where they are and whether they're hostile or Force-sensitive.

Telekinetic Touch: You can perform harmless, subtle effects with the Force at will, such as moving or manipulating a small, unattended object within Close range.

Force Adept Subclasses

Choose either the Jedi or Sith subclass.

JEDI

Play the Jedi if you want to protect others with calm focus and a lightsaber.

Spellcast Trait: Instinct

Foundation Features

Serenity: Once per rest, when you succeed with Hope on a Spellcast Roll, clear a Stress.

Lightsaber Defense: While you wield a lightsaber, when you take damage from a ranged attack, you can mark a Stress instead of an Armor Slot to reduce the severity by one threshold.

Specialization Features

Return Fire: When you use Lightsaber Defense, you can spend a Hope to deflect the bolt at the attacker or another adversary within Close range. Make a Spellcast Roll against them; on a success, deal your lightsaber's damage.

Calm Focus: You can use Serenity twice per rest.

Mastery Feature

Master's Guard: You can use Lightsaber Defense against melee attacks as well as ranged attacks. Additionally, while you wield a lightsaber, allies within Very Close range gain a +1 bonus to their Evasion against ranged attacks.

SITH

Play the Sith if you want to draw power from your passion and dominate your enemies.

Spellcast Trait: Presence

Foundation Features

Passion: When you succeed on an attack or a Spellcast Roll that deals damage, you can mark a Stress to add a number of d6s equal to your tier to the damage roll. If you rolled with Fear, mark an additional Stress.

Dominate: You have advantage on Presence Rolls to intimidate.

Specialization Features

Terrifying Presence: When you succeed on a Presence Roll to intimidate an adversary, they must mark a Stress.

Hungry Darkness: Once per rest, when an adversary within Close range is defeated, clear 2 Stress.

Mastery Feature

Dark Apotheosis: Passion adds d8s instead of d6s. Additionally, once per rest, you can use Passion without marking any Stress.

Character Guide

Suggested Traits: Agility +1, Strength +0, Finesse +1, Instinct +2, Presence +0, Knowledge −1

Suggested Gear: Lightsaber; Jedi Robes

Clothes: Hooded robes, layered wraps, a weathered travel cloak, a black armored tunic, mismatched scavenged gear

Personality: A monk, a hermit, a wildfire, a lighthouse, a storm

Background Questions

  • Who first recognized your connection to the Force, and what did they ask of you in return?

  • What did you leave behind when you chose your path, and do you ever regret it?

  • You've had the same vision more than once. What do you see, and why do you fear it will come true?

Connections

  • What did I sense in you the first time we met?

  • Why don't you fully trust me when I call on the Force?

  • I once used the Force to save your life. What did it cost me?

Force Adept cards

21 cards, from level 1 to 10. Take two level 1 cards at creation, then one new card each time you level up, at your level or lower.

Level 1 Tier 1

Force Push

Level 1 Force Adept Spell · Recall Cost: 1

A sweep of the hand, and the stormtrooper is gone.

Make a Spellcast Roll against a target within Close range. On a success, they're knocked back to Far range and take d8+2 magic damage using your Proficiency.

Mind Trick

Level 1 Force Adept Spell · Recall Cost: 0

A calm voice, a small gesture, and the checkpoint guard waves you through.

Make a Spellcast Roll against a target within Close range who can hear you. On a success, they temporarily accept one simple statement or suggestion you make, as long as it doesn't put them or their allies in obvious danger. When the effect ends, they don't realize they were influenced.

Droids are immune to this spell, and the GM can decide that some strong-willed beings are too.

Force Leap

Level 1 Force Adept Spell · Recall Cost: 1

The Force carries you over the chasm and onto the catwalk above.

Spend a Hope to leap to a point you can see within Far range, including up onto high ledges or across gaps, without making an Agility Roll. If you land within Melee range of an adversary and immediately make an attack against them, gain a +1 bonus to the attack roll.

Level 2 Tier 2

Force Choke

Level 2 Force Adept Spell · Recall Cost: 1

Two fingers close, and their breath stops.

Make a Spellcast Roll against a target within Close range. On a success, you seize them in the Force, dealing 1d20+3 magic damage, and they're temporarily Restrained.

Aggressive Form

Level 2 Force Adept Ability · Recall Cost: 1

You abandon defense and press the attack.

Mark a Stress to gain advantage on an attack.

Level 3 Tier 2

Force Flip

Level 3 Force Adept Ability · Recall Cost: 1

The blade sweeps where you were standing a heartbeat ago.

Once per rest, when a creature within Melee range would deal damage to you, you can avoid the attack and safely flip out of Melee range of them.

Guided Strikes

Level 3 Force Adept Ability · Recall Cost: 1

Let the Force move your hands.

You can use your Spellcast trait for an equipped weapon, rather than the trait the weapon calls for.

When you deal damage, you can mark a Stress to use the maximum result of one of your damage dice instead of rolling it.

Level 4 Tier 2

Force Repulse

Level 4 Force Adept Spell · Recall Cost: 2

A wave of the Force bursts outward, scattering everyone around you.

Make a Spellcast Roll against all targets within Melee range. Targets you succeed against are forced back to Far range and take d8+3 magic damage using your Spellcast trait.

Duelist's Focus

Level 4 Force Adept Ability · Recall Cost: 2

The battle fades. There is only your opponent.

Once per rest, you can turn all your focus toward a target of your choice. Until you attack another creature, you defeat the target, or the battle ends, gain a +1 bonus to your Proficiency.

Level 5 Tier 3

Force Lightning

Level 5 Force Adept Spell · Recall Cost: 1

Blue-white lightning crawls from your fingertips and leaps from body to body.

Mark 2 Stress to make a Spellcast Roll, unleashing lightning on all targets within Close range. Targets you succeed against must make a reaction roll with a Difficulty equal to the result of your Spellcast Roll. Targets who fail take 2d8+4 magic damage.

Additional adversaries not already targeted by Force Lightning and within Close range of previous targets who took damage must also make the reaction roll. Targets who fail take 2d8+4 magic damage. This chain continues until there are no more adversaries within range.

Force Vision

Level 5 Force Adept Spell · Recall Cost: 2

You've already seen how this ends, so you choose differently.

Once per long rest, immediately after the GM conveys the consequences of a roll you made, you can rescind the move and consequences like they never happened and make another move instead.

Level 6 Tier 3

Telekinetic Throw

Level 6 Force Adept Spell · Recall Cost: 0

You lift the trooper off the ground and hurl him into his squad.

Make a Spellcast Roll against a target within Far range. On a success, you can use the Force to move them anywhere within Far range of their original position.

You can throw the lifted target as an attack by making an additional Spellcast Roll against a second target. On a success, deal d12+4 physical damage to the second target using your Proficiency. This spell then ends.

Unleashed Fury

Level 6 Force Adept Ability · Recall Cost: 1

Your anger gives you focus, and your strikes land like hammers.

Before you make an attack, you can mark a Stress to gain a bonus to your damage roll equal to twice your Strength. You can use Unleashed Fury twice per attack.

Level 7 Tier 3

Force Concealment

Level 7 Force Adept Spell · Recall Cost: 2

You fold your presence into the Force until no one can sense you.

When you make a successful Spellcast Roll to cast a different spell, you can spend a Hope to become Cloaked. While Cloaked, you remain unseen if you are stationary when an adversary moves to where they would normally see you. When you move into or within an adversary's line of sight or make an attack, you are no longer Cloaked.

Saber Graze

Level 7 Force Adept Ability · Recall Cost: 1

Even a miss with a lightsaber leaves a mark.

When you fail an attack, you can mark a Stress to deal weapon damage using half your Proficiency.

Level 8 Tier 4

Force Absorb

Level 8 Force Adept Spell · Recall Cost: 1

You catch the lightning in your palm and send it home.

When you would take magic damage, you can spend any number of Hope to roll that many d6s. If any roll a 6, you turn the attack back on its source, dealing the damage to them instead.

Battle Meditation

Level 8 Force Adept Ability · Recall Cost: 2

You close your eyes, and the whole army moves as one.

Once per long rest, you can reach through the Force to steady your allies. All allies within Far range each clear a Stress and gain a Hope. Additionally, your allies gain advantage on attack rolls until you or an ally rolls a failure with Fear.

Level 9 Tier 4

Far Sight

Level 9 Force Adept Spell · Recall Cost: 0

You see a distant place as though you stand in it.

Once per rest, make a Spellcast Roll (15). On a success, drop into a vision that lets you clearly see and hear any place you have been before as though you are standing there in this moment. You can move freely in this vision and are not constrained by a physical body. This spell can't be detected by mundane means. You drop out of this vision when you take damage or cast another spell.

Decisive Strike

Level 9 Force Adept Ability · Recall Cost: 3

One stroke ends the duel.

Once per long rest, spend a Hope to make an attack roll. The GM tells you which targets within range it would succeed against. Choose one of these targets and force them to mark 5 Hit Points.

Level 10 Tier 4

Will of the Force

Level 10 Force Adept Spell · Recall Cost: 1

The galaxy bends, just slightly, to your will.

After you or a willing ally make any roll, you can spend 5 Hope to change the numerical result of that roll to a result of your choice instead. The result must be plausible within the range of the dice.

Force Storm

Level 10 Force Adept Spell · Recall Cost: 1

Debris and lightning tear through the battlefield.

Make a Spellcast Roll against all adversaries within Far range. Mark any number of Stress to unleash a storm of Force-hurled debris and lightning. Targets you succeed against take 1d20+2 magic damage for each Stress marked.

Core Materials›Classes
class portrait

Scout

Scout

Scouts go first into hostile worlds, reading terrain, finding paths, and picking off threats from a distance before anyone else knows they're there.

Starting Evasion
12
Starting Hit Points
6
Class Items
A battered pair of macrobinoculars, or a hand-drawn map of a world that isn't on any navigation chart

Scout's Hope Feature

On the Move: Spend 3 Hope to move to any point within Far range without a roll, even through hazards or past adversaries. One ally within Very Close range can move with you.

Class Features

Read the Land: You have advantage on Instinct Rolls to track creatures, navigate unfamiliar terrain, or sense danger.

Reconnaissance: When you scout an area before entering it, you can spend a Hope to ask the GM one question about its threats, useful terrain, or hidden routes. The GM answers honestly.

Long Shot: When you make a damage roll with a ranged weapon against a target at Far or Very Far range, you can mark a Stress to gain a +1 bonus to your Proficiency.

Scout Subclasses

Choose either the Pathfinder or Recon subclass.

PATHFINDER

Play the Pathfinder if you want to lead your allies safely through the galaxy's most dangerous places.

Spellcast Trait: Instinct

Foundation Features

Trailblazer: When you lead the party through unfamiliar terrain, you find the safest available route without a roll, unless something actively conceals it.

Safe Passage: Once per session, when you guide the party safely through dangerous terrain, you and each ally who followed you clear a Stress.

Specialization Feature

Lead the Way: Allies who follow your lead through dangerous terrain have advantage on rolls to traverse it, including reaction rolls against its hazards.

Mastery Feature

Gone to the Wilds: Once per rest, spend a Hope to slip into the terrain with your allies. You and every ally within Close range become Hidden.

RECON

Play the Recon if you want to find the enemy's weak points and set them up for the kill.

Spellcast Trait: Agility

Foundation Feature

Spotter: When you succeed with Hope on a roll to locate an adversary or identify its weakness, you can mark a Stress to make it temporarily Vulnerable.

Specialization Feature

Painted Target: When an ally hits an adversary you made Vulnerable with Spotter, they add a d6 to their damage roll.

Mastery Feature

Overwatch: When an adversary within Far range makes an attack against an ally, you can mark a Stress to make a ranged attack against it first. If you deal Major damage or more, its attack fails.

Character Guide

Suggested Traits: Agility +2, Strength +0, Finesse +1, Instinct +1, Presence −1, Knowledge +0

Suggested Gear: E-11 Blaster Rifle; Scout Trooper Armor

Clothes: A camouflage poncho, forest fatigues, sun-bleached desert wraps, a cold-weather parka, a helmet with a cracked visor

Personality: A hawk, a wolf, a park ranger, a compass, a shadow

Background Questions

  • Which world taught you how to survive, and what nearly killed you there?

  • You once led people to safety through hostile territory. Who didn't make it, and why?

  • What do you keep scanning the horizon for, even when there's no reason to?

Connections

  • What did you notice about me that nobody else did?

  • I got us lost once. Why won't you let me forget it?

  • What did I teach you about staying alive out there?

Scout cards

21 cards, from level 1 to 10. Take two level 1 cards at creation, then one new card each time you level up, at your level or lower.

Level 1 Tier 1

Bolas

Level 1 Scout Spell · Recall Cost: 1

Weighted cords whistle through the air and wrap around their legs.

Make a Spellcast Roll against a target within Far range. On a success, a hurled bolas or snare net wraps around them, dealing 1d8+1 physical damage and temporarily Restraining the target.

Additionally on a success, you can spend a Hope to temporarily Restrain another adversary within Very Close range of your target.

One with the Wild

Level 1 Scout Ability · Recall Cost: 0

The tauntauns are restless, and you know why.

You can read the creatures and terrain around you. When you want to learn what a wild animal's behavior or the land itself can tell you, make an Instinct Roll (12). On a success, you learn what they can tell you. On a roll with Fear, what you learn might be limited or come at a cost.

Additionally, before you make a Spellcast Roll while within a wild environment, you can spend a Hope to gain a +2 bonus to the roll.

Hard Target

Level 1 Scout Ability · Recall Cost: 1

Always moving, never where they expect.

Gain a bonus to your Evasion equal to half your Agility.

Level 2 Tier 2

Trained Beast

Level 2 Scout Spell · Recall Cost: 1

A whistle, and your convor drops from the canopy onto your shoulder.

Spend a Hope to call a small trained creature (such as a convor, a loth-cat, or a kowakian monkey-lizard) to your side until your next rest, you use Trained Beast again, or the creature is targeted by an attack. If you spend an additional Hope, the creature can fly.

You can communicate with it, make a Spellcast Roll to command it to perform simple tasks, and mark a Stress to see through its eyes. When you deal damage to an adversary within Melee range of your beast, add a d6 to your damage roll.

Recon Plan

Level 2 Scout Ability · Recall Cost: 1

You studied this approach for hours before the shooting started.

After a long rest, place a number of tokens equal to your Knowledge on this card (minimum 1). The first time you move within Close range of an adversary and make an attack against them, you can spend one token to choose one of the following options:

  • You make the attack with advantage.

  • You clear a Stress on an ally within Melee range of the adversary.

  • You add a d8 to your damage roll.

When you take a long rest, clear all unspent tokens.

Level 3 Tier 2

Acid Round

Level 3 Scout Spell · Recall Cost: 1

The round splashes, hisses, and eats through armor plating.

Make a Spellcast Roll against a target within Far range. On a success, deal d6+4 physical damage using your Proficiency.

Additionally, mark 2 or more Stress to make them permanently Corroded. While a target is Corroded, they gain a −1 penalty to their Difficulty for every 2 Stress you spent. This condition can stack.

Field Coordinator

Level 3 Scout Ability · Recall Cost: 1

"Left flank, low ridge. Go now."

When you Help an Ally, they can spend a Hope to add one of your Experiences to their roll alongside your advantage die.

When making a Tag Team Roll, you can roll a d20 as your Hope Die.

Level 4 Tier 2

Snare Line

Level 4 Scout Spell · Recall Cost: 1

A weighted cable snaps out and coils tight.

Make a Spellcast Roll against a target within Close range and choose one of the following options:

  • You pull the target into Melee range or pull yourself into Melee range of them.

  • You constrict the target and force them to mark 2 Stress.

  • All adversaries between you and the target must succeed on a Reaction Roll (13) or be lashed by the cable, taking 3d6+2 physical damage.

On a success, the line wraps around the target, causing the chosen effect and temporarily Restraining them.

Field Remedies

Level 4 Scout Spell · Recall Cost: 2

Crushed roots, boiled moss, and a steady hand.

Once per long rest, you can break out the remedies you've gathered from the wild. You and all allies within Close range clear a Hit Point.

Spend 2 Hope to allow you and all allies to clear 2 Hit Points instead.

Level 5 Tier 3

Study the Target

Level 5 Scout Ability · Recall Cost: 1

Watch long enough, and every hunter shows you its habits.

When observing a creature, you can make an Instinct Roll against them. On a success, spend a Hope and ask the GM for one set of information about the target from the following options:

  • Their unmarked Hit Points and Stress.

  • Their Difficulty and damage thresholds.

  • Their tactics and standard attack damage dice.

  • Their features and Experiences.

Additionally on a success, you can mark a Stress to remove a Fear from the GM's Fear Pool.

Hunker Down

Level 5 Scout Spell · Recall Cost: 1

A foxhole, a camo net, and a lot of rocks.

Make a Spellcast Roll (13). On a success, spend 2 Hope to throw up a camouflaged barricade that you and one ally can take cover within. While inside the barricade, a creature can't be targeted by attacks and can't make attacks. Attacks made against the barricade automatically succeed.

The barricade has the following damage thresholds and lasts until it marks 3 Hit Points. Place tokens on this card to represent marking Hit Points.

Thresholds: 15/30

Level 6 Tier 3

Scavenger

Level 6 Scout Ability · Recall Cost: 1

Every wreck and wasteland has something worth taking.

As an additional downtime move you can choose, roll a d6 to see what you scavenge. Work with the GM to describe it and add it to your inventory as a consumable. Your party can carry up to five scavenged consumables at a time.

  1. A ration bar (clear 2 Stress)

  2. A lucky trinket (gain 2 Hope)

  3. A focus stim (+2 to a Spellcast Roll)

  4. A bacta patch (clear 2 Hit Points)

  5. A good-luck charm (reroll any die)

  6. Choose one of the options above.

Wild Mounts

Level 6 Scout Spell · Recall Cost: 0

Dewbacks, tauntauns, varactyls: you can ride anything.

Spend any number of Hope to find and tame that many riding beasts that you and your allies can ride until your next long rest or the mounts take any damage. The mounts double your land speed while traveling and, when in danger, allow you to move within Far range without having to roll. Creatures riding a mount gain a −2 penalty to attack rolls and a +2 bonus to damage rolls.

Level 7 Tier 3

Adrenaline Surge

Level 7 Scout Spell · Recall Cost: 2

Your heart pounds, and the world slows down.

Once per long rest, mark a Stress to push yourself into a burst of instinct and adrenaline. Place a d6 on this card with the 1 value facing up.

While the Surge Die is active, you add its value to every action roll you make. After you add its value to a roll, increase the Surge Die's value by one. When the die's value would exceed 6 or you take a rest, the surge ends and you must mark an additional Stress.

Marksman's Precision

Level 7 Scout Ability · Recall Cost: 1

Breathe out. Squeeze.

When you make a successful attack with a weapon, gain a bonus to your damage roll equal to either your Finesse or Agility.

Level 8 Tier 4

Weak Point

Level 8 Scout Ability · Recall Cost: 3

Your shot cracks the armor. The next one goes through it.

When you make a successful attack, you can mark a Stress to make the next successful attack against that same target deal an extra 2d12 damage.

Herd Them

Level 8 Scout Ability · Recall Cost: 1

You drive the enemy exactly where you want them.

Make an Agility Roll against all targets within Close range. Spend a Hope to move targets you succeed against, and any willing allies within Close range, to another point within Close range.

Level 9 Tier 4

Survivor

Level 9 Scout Ability · Recall Cost: 1

You've survived worse planets than this one.

When you have 2 or fewer Hit Points unmarked, you don't take Minor damage.

Ricochet Volley

Level 9 Scout Ability · Recall Cost: 3

Shots bounce off rock and durasteel to find every target.

Spend a Hope and make an attack against all adversaries within your weapon's range. Once per long rest, on a success against any targets, add up the damage dealt, then redistribute that damage however you wish between the targets you succeeded against. When you deal damage to a target, roll an additional damage die and add its result to the damage you deal to that target.

Level 10 Tier 4

Through the Line

Level 10 Scout Ability · Recall Cost: 1

You sprint the length of their position, firing the whole way.

Spend 3 Hope to run a straight path through the battlefield to a point within Far range, making an attack against all adversaries within your weapon's range along that path. Choose the order in which you deal damage to the targets you succeeded against. For the first, roll your weapon damage with a +1 bonus to your Proficiency. Then remove a die from your damage roll and deal the remaining damage to the next target. Continue to remove a die for each subsequent target until you have no more damage dice or adversaries.

You can't target the same adversary more than once per attack.

Ghost of the Wilds

Level 10 Scout Ability · Recall Cost: 2

They never land a shot, and every miss makes you calmer.

When an attack made against you fails, clear a Stress. If you can't clear a Stress, gain a Hope.

Core Materials›Classes
class portrait

Scoundrel

Scoundrel

Scoundrels live by their wits, their luck, and a fast blaster, always one bad deal away from a price on their head.

Starting Evasion
11
Starting Hit Points
6
Class Items
A pair of lucky dice on a chain, or a datapad listing everyone you owe

Scoundrel's Hope Feature

Never Tell Me the Odds: Spend 3 Hope after you roll with Fear to count it as a roll with Hope instead. You gain a Hope, and the GM doesn't gain a Fear.

Class Features

Dirty Tricks: When you succeed with Hope on an action roll against an adversary, you can mark a Stress to create an opening. The next ally to make a roll against that adversary gains a +2 bonus.

Lucky Break: Once per rest, when you fail an action roll, you can mark a Stress to treat it as a success with Fear instead.

Scoundrel Subclasses

Choose either the Smuggler or Gunslinger subclass.

SMUGGLER

Play the Smuggler if you want a contact in every port and a talent for getting things where they shouldn't go.

Spellcast Trait: Presence

Foundation Feature

I Know a Guy: Once per session, when you arrive in a settlement, you can establish a contact there. Give them a name and say how you know them. The contact can provide information, an introduction, or a minor service. Until your next long rest, you can use the contact as an Experience (+2) on rolls their help applies to.

Specialization Feature

Friends Everywhere: You can use I Know a Guy twice per session, and your contacts count as an Experience at +3 instead of +2.

Mastery Feature

Smuggler's Run: Once per session, when you try to get your ship, cargo, or crew past a blockade, checkpoint, or search, you can roll a d20 as your Hope Die.

GUNSLINGER

Play the Gunslinger if you want to be the fastest draw in any cantina.

Spellcast Trait: Agility

Foundation Feature

Fast on the Draw: The first time you make an attack roll in a scene, you gain a +2 bonus to the roll.

Specialization Feature

Quick Draw: Fast on the Draw now applies to your first attack roll against each different adversary in a scene.

Mastery Feature

Fan the Hammer: Once per rest, spend a Hope to make an attack against every adversary within Close range. Roll damage separately for each target you hit.

Character Guide

Suggested Traits: Agility +1, Strength −1, Finesse +2, Instinct +0, Presence +1, Knowledge +0

Suggested Gear: DL-44 Heavy Blaster Pistol; Vibroknife; Blast Vest

Clothes: An open-collared shirt and vest, a long spacer's coat, a gun belt with a low-slung holster, a stolen uniform jacket, gaudy jewelry

Personality: A fox, a card shark, a stray cat, a salesman, a rogue planet

Background Questions

  • Who do you owe, how much, and how close are they to collecting?

  • What cargo did you dump or lose that someone powerful still wants back?

  • Who is the one person you would never double-cross, and why?

Connections

  • Why did I bail you out of that cantina brawl?

  • What did I win from you in a game of sabacc, and do you want it back?

  • Why do you trust me, even though you know better?

Scoundrel cards

21 cards, from level 1 to 10. Take two level 1 cards at creation, then one new card each time you level up, at your level or lower.

Level 1 Tier 1

Fast Talker

Level 1 Scoundrel Ability · Recall Cost: 0

"Routine maintenance, officer. You'll want to stand back from that coolant leak."

Spend a Hope to gain advantage on a roll to deceive or bluff someone into believing a lie you tell them.

Light Fingers

Level 1 Scoundrel Ability · Recall Cost: 0

The lock clicks open before the patrol rounds the corner.

You have advantage on action rolls to pick locks, disarm traps, or steal items from a target (either through stealth or by force).

Trick Shot

Level 1 Scoundrel Spell · Recall Cost: 1

The bolt ricochets off a support beam and catches them from behind.

Make a Spellcast Roll against a target within Far range. On a success, spend a Hope to bank a shot off the environment, dealing d8+2 physical damage using your Proficiency. The target becomes temporarily Vulnerable.

Level 2 Tier 2

Gambler's Read

Level 2 Scoundrel Spell · Recall Cost: 1

Everyone has a tell. You've spotted theirs.

Make a Spellcast Roll against a target within Very Close range. On a success, you've read their tells: while they remain within Close range, you know whenever they lie to you, but they are not compelled to speak. If you call out a lie and they refuse to answer, they must mark a Stress and the effect ends. The target is typically unaware they've been read.

Smart Mouth

Level 2 Scoundrel Ability · Recall Cost: 2

You know exactly which buttons to push.

When you taunt or provoke a target within Far range, make a Presence Roll against them. Once per rest on a success, roll a number of d4s equal to your Proficiency. The target must mark Stress equal to the highest result rolled.

Level 3 Tier 2

Flash Bang

Level 3 Scoundrel Spell · Recall Cost: 1

Close your eyes. They didn't.

Make a Spellcast Roll against all adversaries in front of you within Close range. Once per rest on a success, a blinding flash temporarily Stuns targets you succeed against and forces them to mark a Stress. While Stunned, they can't use reactions and can't take any other actions until they clear this condition.

Cheap Shot

Level 3 Scoundrel Ability · Recall Cost: 1

Fighting fair is for people with better odds.

When you position yourself behind a creature who's about your size, you can mark a Stress to grab them in a headlock, making them temporarily Vulnerable.

When a creature attacks a target who is Vulnerable in this way, they deal an extra 2d6 damage.

Level 4 Tier 2

Bugged

Level 4 Scoundrel Spell · Recall Cost: 1

A friendly clap on the shoulder, and now you hear everything.

Choose a target within Very Far range who carries a bug you planted, or slip one onto a target within Melee range now. You can see and hear what they see and hear through the bug, switching freely between their senses and your own, until you use another Spell or until your next rest.

Exploit the Gap

Level 4 Scoundrel Spell · Recall Cost: 1

Right there, between the chest plate and the collar.

Make a Spellcast Roll against a target within Very Close range. On a success, spend a Hope to spot the gaps in their defenses, temporarily reducing the target's Difficulty by a value equal to your Knowledge (minimum 1).

Level 5 Tier 3

Double-Cross

Level 5 Scoundrel Spell · Recall Cost: 1

"Didn't your boss tell you? He's selling you out."

Whisper a convincing lie to an adversary within Melee range and make a Spellcast Roll (13). On a success, the target must mark a Stress and make an attack against another adversary instead of against you or your allies.

Once this attack is over, the target realizes what happened. The next time you use Double-Cross on them, gain a −5 penalty to the Spellcast Roll.

Read the Table

Level 5 Scoundrel Spell · Recall Cost: 2

You can see what they're planning before they do.

Spend a Hope to read the surface intentions of a target within Far range from their body language. Make a Spellcast Roll against the target to read deeper, more hidden intentions.

On a roll with Fear, the target might, at the GM's discretion, notice you sizing them up.

Level 6 Tier 3

Payback

Level 6 Scoundrel Ability · Recall Cost: 2

Nobody shoots you and walks away.

When you mark 1 or more Hit Points from an attack, you can mark a Stress to place a number of tokens equal to the number of Hit Points you marked on this card. On your next successful attack, gain a +5 bonus to your damage roll for each token on this card, then clear all tokens.

Take the Heat

Level 6 Scoundrel Spell · Recall Cost: 0

A bad joke and a worse plan, and somehow everyone feels better.

Once per rest, take on the Stress from a willing creature within Melee range. The target shares what's really weighing on them. Transfer any number of their marked Stress to you, then gain a Hope for each Stress transferred.

Level 7 Tier 3

Charm Offensive

Level 7 Scoundrel Ability · Recall Cost: 1

That smile has gotten you out of worse.

After you make an action roll to persuade, lie, or garner favor, you can spend a Hope to reroll the Hope or Fear Die.

Now You See Me

Level 7 Scoundrel Spell · Recall Cost: 1

The shot goes wide, and by the time the smoke clears, you're gone.

When an attack made against you that would deal physical damage fails, you can spend a Hope to dive out of sight, becoming Hidden and moving to a point within Close range of the attacker. You remain Hidden until the next time you make an action roll.

Level 8 Tier 4

Showstopper

Level 8 Scoundrel Spell · Recall Cost: 3

Every eye in the cantina is on you, and nobody's watching the door.

Make a Spellcast Roll against all targets within Far range. Targets you succeed against become temporarily Captivated. While Captivated, a target's attention is fixed on you, narrowing their field of view and drowning out any sound but your voice. Mark a Stress to force all Captivated targets to mark a Stress, ending this spell.

Shadow Dweller

Level 8 Scoundrel Ability · Recall Cost: 2

Back alleys and blackouts are home turf.

While you're in low light or darkness, you gain a +1 bonus to your Evasion and make attack rolls with advantage.

Level 9 Tier 4

Seen It All

Level 9 Scoundrel Ability · Recall Cost: 0

Hokey tricks and lucky shots, you've done them all twice.

Gain a permanent +2 bonus to two of your Experiences or a permanent +3 bonus to one of your Experiences. Then place this card in your vault permanently.

Long Con

Level 9 Scoundrel Ability · Recall Cost: 1

Every move you make is setting up the last one.

Choose a target within Far range. When you succeed on an action roll against them that doesn't result in making a damage roll, place a token on this card. When you deal damage to this target, spend any number of tokens to add a d12 for each token spent to your damage roll. You can only run the Long Con on one creature at a time.

When you choose a new target or take a rest, clear all unspent tokens.

Level 10 Tier 4

Infamous

Level 10 Scoundrel Ability · Recall Cost: 0

Every spaceport knows your name, and half of them want you dead.

People know who you are and what you've done, and they treat you differently because of it. When you leverage your notoriety to get what you want, you can mark a Stress before you roll to gain a +10 bonus to the result. Your food and drinks are always free wherever you go, and everything else you buy is reduced in price by one bag of credits (to a minimum of one handful).

This card doesn't count against your loadout's maximum of 5 cards and can't be placed in your vault.

Double Tap

Level 10 Scoundrel Spell · Recall Cost: 1

Your partner fires, and you fire right behind them.

When an ally within Close range deals damage to an adversary, you can make a Spellcast Roll against that same target. On a success, you deal the same damage to the target that your ally dealt. If your Spellcast Roll succeeds with Fear, place this card in your vault.

Core Materials›Classes
class portrait

Guardian

Guardian

Guardians stand between their allies and the blaster fire, from sworn Royal Guards to loyal Wookiee warriors and armored protectors.

Starting Evasion
9
Starting Hit Points
7
Class Items
A token from someone you swore to protect, or a scarred armor plate from your first battle

Guardian's Hope Feature

Stand Your Ground: Spend 3 Hope to gain resistance to physical damage until an attack succeeds against you or you take a rest.

Class Features

Protector: When an ally within Very Close range is targeted by an attack, you can mark a Stress to become the target instead.

Brawn: You have advantage on Strength Rolls to lift, push, carry, break, or physically restrain.

Guardian Subclasses

Choose either the Champion or Bodyguard subclass. Guardian subclasses have no Spellcast trait.

CHAMPION

Play the Champion if you want to drive enemies back with overwhelming force.

Foundation Feature

Relentless Warrior: When you succeed on a Melee attack, you can mark a Stress to choose one: the target marks a Stress, or you knock them back to Close range.

Specialization Feature

Unstoppable Momentum: When you use Relentless Warrior, you can choose both options.

Mastery Feature

Champion's Roar: Once per long rest, you can let out a thunderous battle roar. All adversaries within Close range mark a Stress, and all allies within Close range clear a Stress.

BODYGUARD

Play the Bodyguard if you want to take the hits meant for the people you protect.

Foundation Feature

Living Shield: When you use your Protector feature, reduce the severity of the damage you take from that attack by one threshold.

Specialization Feature

Ever Vigilant: You can use Protector on an ally within Close range instead of Very Close range. When you do, you move into Melee range of them.

Mastery Feature

Last Line: Once per long rest, when an ally within Close range would mark their last Hit Point, you can take that damage instead and reduce its severity by two thresholds.

Character Guide

Suggested Traits: Agility +0, Strength +2, Finesse −1, Instinct +1, Presence +1, Knowledge +0

Suggested Gear: Vibroaxe, or a Vibrosword with a Riot Shield; Clone Trooper Armor

Clothes: Crimson ceremonial robes over armor, a heavy bandolier, battered armor plates, a thick cloak, a guard's helmet with the insignia scratched off

Personality: A mountain, a guard dog, an older sibling, a wall, an oak tree

Background Questions

  • Who did you fail to protect, and what do you do differently because of it?

  • What oath did you swear, and to whom?

  • Who taught you to fight, and what became of them?

Connections

  • Why did I step in front of a blaster bolt meant for you?

  • What do you keep doing that makes my job harder?

  • What promise did I make to you, and have I kept it?

Guardian cards

21 cards, from level 1 to 10. Take two level 1 cards at creation, then one new card each time you level up, at your level or lower.

Level 1 Tier 1

Grit Your Teeth

Level 1 Guardian Ability · Recall Cost: 1

The bolt scorches your armor, and you keep coming.

When you take Severe damage, you can mark a Stress to reduce the severity by one threshold.

Bull Rush

Level 1 Guardian Ability · Recall Cost: 0

Shoulder down, straight through the line.

Make an attack with your primary weapon against a target within Melee range. On a success, you deal damage and knock them back to Close range. On a success with Hope, add a d6 to your damage roll.

Additionally, you can spend a Hope to make them temporarily Vulnerable.

Who needs armor when you're built like a Wookiee?

When you choose not to equip armor, you have a base Armor Score of 3 + your Strength and use the following as your base damage thresholds:

  • Tier 1: 9/19

  • Tier 2: 11/24

  • Tier 3: 13/31

  • Tier 4: 15/38

Heavy Hitter

Level 2 Guardian Ability · Recall Cost: 1

Every swing carries your full weight behind it.

On a successful attack using a weapon with a Melee range, gain a bonus to your damage roll equal to your Strength.

Imposing

Level 2 Guardian Ability · Recall Cost: 0

You don't need to say much. You loom.

When you make a Presence Roll, you can spend a Hope to add your Strength to the roll.

Additionally, once per rest when you would gain a condition, you can describe how your sheer presence carries you through the situation and avoid gaining the condition.

Level 3 Tier 2

I've Got You

Level 3 Guardian Ability · Recall Cost: 1

A hand on the shoulder, and they're back on their feet.

Once per long rest, when you console or encourage an ally who failed an action roll, you can both clear 2 Stress.

Weapons Expert

Level 3 Guardian Ability · Recall Cost: 1

Vibro-axe, force pike, or a bent pipe: you know how to use it.

When you deal damage, you can mark a Stress to use the maximum result of one of your damage dice instead of rolling it.

Level 4 Tier 2

Come and Get It

Level 4 Guardian Ability · Recall Cost: 1

A roar, a bang on your shield, and every gun turns toward you.

Describe how you taunt a target within Close range, then make a Presence Roll against them. On a success, the target must mark a Stress, and the next time the GM spotlights them, they must target you with an attack, which they make with disadvantage.

Reinforced Plating

Level 4 Guardian Ability · Recall Cost: 0

You've welded extra durasteel over the weak spots.

While you're wearing armor, gain a +2 bonus to your damage thresholds.

Level 5 Tier 3

Armorer

Level 5 Guardian Ability · Recall Cost: 1

You keep everyone's armor in fighting shape.

While you're wearing armor, gain a +1 bonus to your Armor Score.

During a rest, when you choose to repair your armor as a downtime move, your allies also clear an Armor Slot.

Iron Constitution

Level 5 Guardian Ability · Recall Cost: 0

It takes a lot more than that to put you down.

When you choose this card, permanently gain two of the following benefits:

  • One Stress slot

  • One Hit Point slot

  • +2 bonus to your damage thresholds

Then place this card in your vault permanently.

Level 6 Tier 3

Unbowed

Level 6 Guardian Ability · Recall Cost: 2

Every wound only makes you steadier.

When you mark 1 or more Hit Points from an attack, clear a Stress.

Berserker Fury

Level 6 Guardian Ability · Recall Cost: 1

A howl rips out of you, and your next blow could tear off an arm.

Level 7 Tier 3

Walk It Off

Level 7 Guardian Ability · Recall Cost: 1

"It's just a scratch." It isn't.

When you would take damage, you can mark a Stress to reduce the severity of the damage by one threshold. When you do, roll a d6. On a result of 3 or lower, place this card in your vault.

Heavy Swing

Level 7 Guardian Ability · Recall Cost: 1

Even a glancing blow from you leaves a dent.

When you fail an attack, you can mark a Stress to deal weapon damage using half your Proficiency.

Level 8 Tier 4

Shockwave Slam

Level 8 Guardian Ability · Recall Cost: 2

You hit the deck so hard the plating buckles.

Spend 2 Hope to strike the ground where you stand and make a Strength Roll against all targets within Very Close range. Targets you succeed against are thrown back to Far range and must make a Reaction Roll (17). Targets who fail take 4d10+8 damage. Targets who succeed take half damage.

Berserk

Level 8 Guardian Ability · Recall Cost: 3

Nothing gets through. Nothing walks away.

Once per long rest, you can go berserk until there are no more adversaries within sight.

While berserk, you can't use Armor Slots, and you gain a +10 bonus to your damage rolls and a +8 bonus to your Severe damage threshold.

Level 9 Tier 4

Immovable

Level 9 Guardian Ability · Recall Cost: 1

You plant your feet. This is as far as they go.

Describe the defensive stance you take and spend a Hope. If an adversary moves within Very Close range, they're pulled into Melee range and Restrained.

This condition lasts until you move or fail a roll with Fear, or the GM spends 2 Fear on their turn to clear it.

Glory of Battle

Level 9 Guardian Ability · Recall Cost: 2

Each foe you drop fills you with fire.

When you critically succeed on a weapon attack, gain an additional Hope or clear an additional Stress.

Additionally, when you deal enough damage to defeat an enemy, gain a Hope or clear a Stress.

Level 10 Tier 4

Not Today

Level 10 Guardian Ability · Recall Cost: 4

They thought you were finished. They were wrong.

When you mark your last Hit Point, instead of making a death move, you can roll a d6 and clear a number of Hit Points equal to the result. Then place this card in your vault.

Juggernaut

Level 10 Guardian Ability · Recall Cost: 3

Every hit lands like a falling starship.

When you successfully make an attack with your weapon, you never deal damage beneath a target's Major damage threshold (the target always marks a minimum of 2 Hit Points).

Additionally, when a creature within your weapon's range deals damage to an ally with an attack that doesn't include you, you can mark a Stress to force them to make a Reaction Roll (15). On a failure, the target must mark a Hit Point.

Pilot

Pilot

Pilots have reflexes faster than thought and the nerve to fly where no one else will, whether they're behind the stick or dodging blaster fire on foot.

Starting Evasion
11
Starting Hit Points
6
Class Items
A lucky charm that hangs in every cockpit you fly, or the helmet of a wingmate who didn't come back

Pilot's Hope Feature

Impossible Maneuver: Spend 3 Hope to automatically succeed on an Agility Roll to maneuver, whether you're on foot or piloting a vehicle. You roll no dice and don't generate Hope or Fear.

Class Features

Ace Pilot: You have advantage on rolls to pilot or maneuver a vehicle.

Evasive: When an attack against you or a vehicle you're piloting succeeds, you can mark a Stress to roll a d4 and add the result to the Evasion against that attack. At level 5, roll a d6 instead.

Maneuver: When you succeed with Hope on a roll to pilot a vehicle, you can also move it up to one additional range.

Pilot Subclasses

Choose either the Hotshot or Wingmate subclass.

HOTSHOT

Play the Hotshot if you want to push every machine past its limits.

Spellcast Trait: Agility

Foundation Feature

Push the Limit: After you see the result of a roll to pilot a vehicle or an Agility Roll to maneuver, you can mark a Stress to gain a +2 bonus to the result.

Specialization Feature

Redline: Push the Limit's bonus increases to +3. Once per rest, you can use it without marking a Stress.

Mastery Feature

Legendary Flyer: Your Impossible Maneuver Hope Feature costs 2 Hope instead of 3.

WINGMATE

Play the Wingmate if you want to keep your allies alive in the thick of the fight.

Spellcast Trait: Presence

Foundation Feature

Covering Fire: When an ally within Close range of you or your vehicle is targeted by an attack, you can spend a Hope to give them a +2 bonus to their Evasion against that attack.

Specialization Feature

Tight Formation: Covering Fire's bonus increases to +3.

Mastery Feature

Squadron Leader: Once per long rest, you and every ally within Far range, along with any vehicles you're piloting, gain a +2 bonus to Evasion until an attack succeeds against each of you or the scene ends.

Character Guide

Suggested Traits: Agility +2, Strength −1, Finesse +1, Instinct +1, Presence +0, Knowledge +0

Suggested Gear: DH-17 Blaster Pistol; Grapnel Launcher; Flight Suit

Clothes: An orange flight suit, a scuffed helmet with custom paint, a leather jacket over a jumpsuit, a squadron patch, goggles pushed up on the forehead

Personality: A comet, a daredevil, a hummingbird, a race announcer, a firecracker

Your ship is a story choice made with the GM, using the Player Ships table in the Starships and Space Combat chapter.

Background Questions

  • What ship do you call home, or which one do you dream of flying?

  • Who taught you to fly, and what did they tell you never to do?

  • What maneuver made your name, and who still talks about it?

Connections

  • Why will you only fly with me as your copilot?

  • What did I break the last time you let me take the controls?

  • When did I fly us out of a situation everyone said was hopeless?

Pilot cards

21 cards, from level 1 to 10. Take two level 1 cards at creation, then one new card each time you level up, at your level or lower.

Level 1 Tier 1

Punch It

Level 1 Pilot Ability · Recall Cost: 0

Throttle to the stops, straight through the gap.

Once per rest, mark a Stress to sprint, or to push a vehicle you're piloting, anywhere within Far range without making a roll to get there. If you immediately make an attack at the end of this movement, with your own weapon or your vehicle's, gain a +1 bonus to the attack roll.

Your voice crackles over the comm: "Steady. Hold your line."

Taunting Flyby

You buzz their position close enough to read their name tags.

When you taunt or provoke a target within Far range, on foot or from the cockpit, make a Presence Roll against them. Once per rest on a success, roll a number of d4s equal to your Proficiency. The target must mark Stress equal to the highest result rolled.

Level 2 Pilot Ability · Recall Cost: 1

You plotted the attack run before you ever left the hangar.

  • You make the attack with advantage.

  • You clear a Stress on an ally within Melee range of the adversary.

  • You add a d8 to your damage roll.

When you take a long rest, clear all unspent tokens.

Call the Shots

"Break left on my mark. Mark!"

When making a Tag Team Roll, you can roll a d20 as your Hope Die.

Brace for Impact

Level 3 Pilot Ability · Recall Cost: 1

Angle the deflectors, grit your teeth, and take the hit.

Crossfire

Level 4 Pilot Ability · Recall Cost: 1

You juke at the last second, and their shot hits their own wingman.

When an attack made from beyond Melee range against you or a vehicle you're piloting fails, roll a number of d6s equal to your Proficiency. If any roll a 6, you can mark a Stress to redirect the attack to damage an adversary within Very Close range instead.

Daredevil Leap

Level 4 Pilot Ability · Recall Cost: 1

A running jump off your friend's shoulders, and you land shooting.

Mark a Stress to boost off a willing ally within Close range, fling yourself into the air, and perform an aerial attack against a target within Far range. You have advantage on the attack, add a d10 to the damage roll, and end your move within Melee range of the target.

Signature Maneuver

Every ace has one move everyone talks about.

Name and describe your signature maneuver. Once per rest, when you perform this maneuver as part of an action you're taking, on foot or at the controls, you can roll a d20 as your Hope Die. On a success, clear a Stress.

Read Their Flying

Level 5 Pilot Ability · Recall Cost: 1

You've watched them long enough to know their next move.

When observing a creature or vehicle, you can make an Instinct Roll against them. On a success, spend a Hope and ask the GM for one set of information about the target from the following options:

  • Their unmarked Hit Points and Stress.

  • Their Difficulty and damage thresholds.

  • Their tactics and standard attack damage dice.

  • Their features and Experiences.

Additionally on a success, you can mark a Stress to remove a Fear from the GM's Fear Pool.

Showoff

Level 6 Pilot Ability · Recall Cost: 2

Getting hit just makes you want to win harder.

When you mark 1 or more Hit Points from an attack, you can mark a Stress to place a number of tokens equal to the number of Hit Points you marked on this card. On your next successful attack, gain a +5 bonus to your damage roll for each token on this card, then clear all tokens.

Quick Turnaround

Level 6 Pilot Ability · Recall Cost: 1

Refuel, rearm, and back in the air before the coffee's cold.

During a short rest, you can choose a long rest downtime move instead. You can spend a Hope to let an ally do the same.

Level 7 Tier 3

Flyboy Charm

Level 7 Pilot Ability · Recall Cost: 1

Nobody stays mad at you for long.

After you make an action roll to persuade, lie, or garner favor, you can spend a Hope to reroll the Hope or Fear Die.

Your shots land exactly where you meant them to.

Evac Run

"Everybody in! Now!"

Make an Agility Roll against all targets within Close range. Spend a Hope to move targets you succeed against, and any willing allies within Close range, to another point within Close range.

Strafing Pass

Level 8 Pilot Ability · Recall Cost: 3

Your first pass cracks their shields. Your second pass finishes the job.

Level 9 Tier 4

Running on Fumes

Half your systems are sparking, and you're still flying.

Few pilots alive can match you.

Level 10 Tier 4

Trench Run

Level 10 Pilot Ability · Recall Cost: 1

One straight shot down the length of their defenses.

Spend 3 Hope to make a straight run through the battlefield, on foot or in a vehicle you're piloting, to a point within Far range, making an attack against all adversaries within your weapon's range along that path. Untouchable Ace

Level 10 Pilot Ability · Recall Cost: 2

Every miss is another reason to grin.
