Tier 1 Minion

A hooded fanatic devoted to the dark side, guarding a relic or serving a master who sees them as fodder.

Motives & Tactics: Chant, guard the relic, overwhelm, sacrifice themselves

Difficulty: 10 | Thresholds: None | HP: 1 | Stress: 1

ATK: −1 | Ritual Blade: Melee | 2 phy

Minion (3) Passive The Cultist is defeated when they take any damage. For every 3 damage a PC deals to the Cultist, defeat an additional Minion within range the attack would succeed against.

Group Attack Action Spend a Fear to choose a target and spotlight all Dark Side Cultists within Close range of them. Those Minions move into Melee range of the target and make one shared attack roll. On a success, they deal 2 physical damage each. Combine this damage.

Dark Devotion Reaction When a Cultist is defeated within Close range of a Force-using ally, that ally clears a Stress.

Inspired by: the dark side cults of Star Wars: Doctor Aphra (comic) and Star Wars: Darth Vader (comic)

Inquisitor

Tier 2 Leader

A dark side agent of the Empire with a spinning double-bladed lightsaber, hunting surviving Jedi across the galaxy.

Motives & Tactics: Hunt Jedi, intimidate, tempt, command troopers

Difficulty: 15 | Thresholds: 11/22 | HP: 7 | Stress: 5

ATK: +4 | Spinning Lightsaber: Very Close | 2d10+4 mag

Experience: Jedi Hunter +3, Intimidation +3

Spinning Blade Action Mark a Stress to make an attack against all targets within Very Close range. Targets the Inquisitor succeeds against take 2d8+4 magic damage.

Saber Throw Action Make an attack against a target within Far range. On a success, deal 2d8+3 magic damage. The saber returns to the Inquisitor's hand.

Force Choke Action Spend a Fear. A target within Close range must succeed on a Strength Reaction Roll (15) or become Restrained and mark 2 Stress.

Command the Hunt Action Spend 2 Fear to spotlight the Inquisitor and up to 2d4 allies within Far range.

Momentum Reaction When the Inquisitor makes a successful attack against a PC, you gain a Fear.

Source: Star Wars Rebels; Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order; Obi-Wan Kenobi

Sith Acolyte

Tier 2 Skulk

A dark side adept with a crimson lightsaber, striking from the shadows to prove their worth to a master.

Motives & Tactics: Ambush, feed on fear, prove themselves, tempt

Difficulty: 14 | Thresholds: 9/18 | HP: 4 | Stress: 4

ATK: +3 | Lightsaber: Melee | 2d8+4 mag

Experience: Stealth +2, Sith Lore +2

Out of Nowhere Passive The Acolyte has advantage on attacks while Hidden.

Force Leap Action Mark a Stress to leap to any point within Far range, then make a standard attack.

Feed on Fear Reaction When a PC within Close range marks Stress, the Acolyte clears a Stress.

Variant: Nightsisters trade Force Leap for Dark Magick Action spend a Fear; a target within Far range must succeed on an Instinct Reaction Roll (14) or become temporarily Vulnerable and mark a Stress.

Inspired by: Savage Opress and Asajj Ventress in Star Wars: The Clone Wars

Darth Vader

Tier 4 Solo

The Dark Lord of the Sith and the Emperor's enforcer, an unstoppable force of armor, anger, and the Force.

Motives & Tactics: Advance without pause, crush hope, hunt Jedi, serve the Emperor

Difficulty: 21 | Thresholds: 38/70 | HP: 12 | Stress: 8

ATK: +8 | Lightsaber: Melee | 4d12+14 mag

Experience: Dueling +5, Intimidation +5

Relentless (3) Passive Vader can be spotlighted up to three times per GM turn. Spend Fear as usual to spotlight him.

Unstoppable Passive Vader can't be knocked back, Restrained, or made Vulnerable. He deflects blaster bolts: ranged physical attacks against him have disadvantage.

Force Choke Action Spend a Fear. A target within Far range must succeed on a Strength Reaction Roll (21) or become Restrained and mark 3 Stress.

Hallway Massacre Action Spend 2 Fear to attack every target within Close range. Targets he succeeds against take 4d10+12 magic damage.

Dread Breathing Passive When Vader enters a scene, each PC must succeed on a Presence Reaction Roll (19) or mark a Stress.

Momentum Reaction When Vader makes a successful attack against a PC, you gain a Fear.

Source: Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope; Rogue One: A Star Wars Story; Obi-Wan Kenobi

Sith Lord

Tier 4 Solo

A Dark Lord of the Sith at the height of their power: the villain at the end of the campaign.

Motives & Tactics: Corrupt, dominate, punish failure, crush hope

Difficulty: 20 | Thresholds: 34/62 | HP: 10 | Stress: 8

ATK: +8 | Lightsaber: Melee | 4d10+12 mag

Experience: Dark Side Mastery +4, Intimidation +4

Relentless (3) Passive The Sith Lord can be spotlighted up to three times per GM turn. Spend Fear as usual to spotlight them.

Aura of Dread Passive PCs within Close range of the Sith Lord can't spend Hope to use Experiences.

Deflect Reaction When a ranged attack targets the Sith Lord, mark a Stress to make it fail.

Force Choke Action A target within Far range must succeed on a Strength Reaction Roll (20) or become Restrained and mark 3 Stress.

Force Lightning Action Spend a Fear. Each target within Close range must make a Reaction Roll (20). Targets who fail take 4d8+12 magic damage and mark a Stress. Targets who succeed take half damage.

Dark Side Ascendant Reaction The first time the Sith Lord would mark their last Hit Point, spend 2 Fear. Instead, they clear 4 Hit Points, and their standard attack deals an extra 1d10 damage for the rest of the scene.

Momentum Reaction When the Sith Lord makes a successful attack against a PC, you gain a Fear.

Inspired by: Darth Sidious and Darth Vader in the prequel and original trilogies

Jedi Padawan

Tier 1 Standard

A Jedi apprentice still learning the ways of the Force: quick, brave, and more reckless than their master would like.

Motives & Tactics: Prove themselves, protect the innocent, follow their master, rush in

Difficulty: 12 | Thresholds: 7/13 | HP: 5 | Stress: 3

ATK: +2 | Lightsaber: Melee | 1d10+3 mag

Experience: Jedi Training +2

Deflect Reaction When the Padawan is targeted by a ranged physical attack, mark a Stress to give the attack disadvantage.

Force Push Action Mark a Stress to shove a target within Close range back to Far range. The target must succeed on a Strength Reaction Roll (12) or become Vulnerable until their next action.

Eager to Prove Passive While the Padawan’s master is within Close range, the Padawan’s attacks have advantage.

Source: Star Wars: The Clone Wars; Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order

Jedi Knight

Tier 3 Solo

A Jedi Knight standing against the party: a hunter of dark siders, a rival from the Order, or a Jedi who has lost their way.

Motives & Tactics: Deflect, disarm, protect the innocent, end the fight without killing

Difficulty: 17 | Thresholds: 20/34 | HP: 9 | Stress: 6

ATK: +5 | Lightsaber: Melee | 3d10+5 mag

Experience: Lightsaber Forms +3, Force Sense +3

Relentless (2) Passive The Jedi can be spotlighted up to two times per GM turn. Spend Fear as usual to spotlight them.

Deflect Reaction When a ranged attack targets the Jedi, mark a Stress to make it fail. If the attacker is within Close range, they take 2d8+3 physical damage from their own deflected bolt.

Force Push Action Make an attack against all targets within Close range. Targets the Jedi succeeds against are knocked back to Far range and take 3d6+3 magic damage.

Mind Trick Action Spend a Fear. A target within Close range must succeed on an Instinct Reaction Roll (17) or be unable to attack the Jedi until the end of the scene or until the Jedi attacks them.

Inspired by: the Jedi of Star Wars: Episodes I–III and Star Wars: The Clone Wars

Jedi Master

Tier 4 Solo

A master of the Jedi Order, calm as still water and decades deep in the Force: a general of the Clone Wars, a hidden survivor, or a teacher who will not let the party pass.

Motives & Tactics: Defend, disarm, read intentions, end the fight without killing, protect the Order’s secrets

Difficulty: 20 | Thresholds: 30/56 | HP: 10 | Stress: 7

ATK: +7 | Lightsaber: Melee | 4d10+12 mag

Experience: Jedi Lore +4, Insight +4

Relentless (2) Passive The Jedi Master can be spotlighted up to two times per GM turn. Spend Fear as usual to spotlight them.

Soresu Guard Passive Ranged physical attacks against the Jedi Master have disadvantage.

Redirect Reaction When a ranged physical attack against the Jedi Master fails, mark a Stress to send the bolt back: the attacker takes the attack’s damage.

Force Wave Action Spend a Fear. Every target within Close range must succeed on a Strength Reaction Roll (20) or take 4d8+10 magic damage, be pushed to Far range, and become Vulnerable until their next action.

Mind Trick Action Mark a Stress. A target within Close range must succeed on an Instinct Reaction Roll (20) or lower their weapon and stop fighting until they take damage or the scene changes. Droids are immune.

Foresight Reaction Once per scene, when an attack would succeed against the Jedi Master, spend a Fear to make it fail instead.

Source: Star Wars: The Clone Wars; Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace

ATK: +1 | War Club: Melee | 1d10+3 phy

Bone-Shaking Blow Action Mark a Stress to attack a target within Melee range. On a success, deal 1d10+4 physical damage and knock them back to Close range.

Source: Star Wars: The Clone Wars; Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order

ATK: +2 | Grasping Claws: Melee | 2d6+3 phy

Already Dead Passive The Revenants are immune to fear and Presence effects and never mark Stress from them.

Rise Again Reaction While a Nightsister Witch is within Far range, the first time the Revenants are defeated in a scene, spend a Fear to have them clear 3 Hit Points.

Vanish Action Mark a Stress to become Hidden, even while observed, until the Witch attacks.

Raise the Dead Action Spend 2 Fear to bring a Nightsister Revenants Horde into the scene at Close range.

VariantAdded feature

Geonosian Warrior Swarm

Tier 1 Horde (1/HP)

Winged Geonosian drones pouring out of hive spires with sonic blasters.

Motives & Tactics: Swarm from above, strafe, defend the hive, obey the queen

Difficulty: 12 | Thresholds: 6/11 | HP: 5 | Stress: 2

ATK: +1 | Sonic Blasters: Far | 1d8+3 phy

Horde (1d4+2) Passive When the Swarm has marked half or more of its HP, its standard attack deals 1d4+2 physical damage instead.

Winged Passive The Swarm can fly. Attacks against it from Melee range have disadvantage unless the attacker can also reach the air.

Hive Defenders Passive While within sight of their hive or queen, the Swarm's attacks have advantage.

Source: Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones

Umbaran Militia

Tier 2 Standard

Pale-eyed Umbaran soldiers fighting in total darkness with advanced weapons and hover tanks.

Motives & Tactics: Strike in the dark, lure into traps, use superior tech

Difficulty: 14 | Thresholds: 10/20 | HP: 5 | Stress: 3

ATK: +2 | Umbaran Rifle: Far | 2d8+4 phy

Night Eyes Passive The Militia sees normally in darkness. In darkness, its attacks have advantage.

Mine Field Action Spend a Fear to place electro-mines in an area within Far range. The first creature to enter it must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll (14) or take 2d10+3 physical damage and become Restrained until the end of their next action.

Source: Star Wars: The Clone Wars

Geonosian Queen

Tier 3 Leader

The massive matriarch of a Geonosian hive, controlling her drones and the dead through brain worms.

Motives & Tactics: Command the hive, spread the worms, protect the eggs, never surrender

Difficulty: 17 | Thresholds: 21/36 | HP: 8 | Stress: 5

ATK: +2 | Mandibles: Very Close | 3d8+4 phy

Experience: Hive Mind +4

Immobile Bulk Passive The Queen can't move from her throne chamber, and when she takes physical damage, reduce it by 3.

Summon the Hive Action Spend 2 Fear to bring a Geonosian Warrior Swarm and 1d4+2 Brain Worm Thralls into the scene at Close range.

Worm Command Action Spend a Fear. A creature infested by a brain worm within Far range must succeed on an Instinct Reaction Roll (17) or make one attack against an ally of the Queen's choice.

Momentum Reaction When the Queen's minions make a successful attack against a PC, you gain a Fear.

Source: Star Wars: The Clone Wars

Mandalorian Rocketeer

Tier 1 Ranged

A clan fighter who lives in the air, raining blaster fire and wrist rockets from a jetpack.

Motives & Tactics: Take the high ground, strafe, harass, fly circles around the enemy

Difficulty: 12 | Thresholds: 7/13 | HP: 4 | Stress: 3

ATK: +1 | Blaster Pistol: Far | 1d8+3 phy

Experience: Jetpack Pilot +2

Jetpack Passive The Rocketeer flies, and can move anywhere within Far range as part of an action.

Wrist Rocket Action Mark a Stress. Each creature within Very Close range of a point within Far range must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll (12) or take 1d10+3 physical damage.

Beskar Helm Reaction When the Rocketeer would take Severe damage, mark a Stress to take Major damage instead.

Source: Star Wars Rebels; The Mandalorian

Mandalorian Warrior

Tier 2 Standard

A warrior in beskar armor and a T-visored helmet, carrying the weapons and the Creed of their clan.

Motives & Tactics: Fly in, honor the Creed, protect the clan, strike hard

Difficulty: 14 | Thresholds: 11/22 | HP: 5 | Stress: 4

ATK: +3 | Heavy Blaster Pistol: Far | 2d8+4 phy

Experience: Creed +2, Tactics +2

Beskar Armor Passive When the Mandalorian takes magic damage, reduce it by 5.

Jetpack Action Mark a Stress to fly to any point within Far range, then make a standard attack.

Vambrace Arsenal Action Mark a Stress and choose one: a flamethrower (each target in front within Close range must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll (14) or take 2d6+3 physical damage), a whipcord (make an attack against a target within Close range; on a success, they're Restrained), or a wrist rocket (make an attack against a target within Far range; on a success, deal 2d8+3 physical damage to them and each creature within Very Close range of them).

Source: The Mandalorian; Star Wars: The Clone Wars; Star Wars Rebels

Clan Armorer

The forge-keeper of a covert, who shapes beskar for the clan’s warriors and fights with hammer and tongs when the forge is threatened.

Molten Beskar Action Mark a Stress to fling molten metal at a target within Close range. On a success, deal 2d8+3 physical damage and the target marks a Stress.

Jetpack Action Mark a Stress to fly to a point within Far range. Its next attack has advantage.

Variant: Beskar Commando. Moff Gideon's commandos in beskar-alloy armor. Tier 3 Standard; Difficulty 17; Thresholds 20/32; HP 6; Stress 4; ATK +3; Blaster Pistols 3d8+4 phy. Add Beskar Alloy - Passive: Reduce magic damage from lightsabers by half.

Dive Strike Action Mark a Stress to fly into Melee range of a target within Far range and attack them. On a success, deal 2d10+4 physical damage and the target is Vulnerable until their next action.

Bodyguard Reaction When an ally within Close range is targeted by an attack, mark a Stress to become the target instead.

Rally the Clan Action Spend a Fear to spotlight the Chieftain and up to 1d4 Mandalorian allies within Far range. Their attacks this spotlight have advantage.

Challenge Action Mark a Stress to call out a PC within Far range. Until the scene ends, the Chieftain’s attacks against that PC have advantage, and that PC’s attacks against anyone else have disadvantage.

Mandalorian Super Commando

Tier 3 Leader

A veteran Mandalorian commander whose squad moves like a single weapon.

Jetpack Strike Action Mark a Stress to fly to any point within Far range, then make a standard attack with advantage.

Jetpack Action Mark a Stress to fly to any point within Far range.

Binders Action Make an attack against a Vulnerable target within Melee range. On a success, the target is Restrained until they break free with a successful Strength or Finesse Roll.

Source: The Mandalorian; Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back

Out of Nowhere Passive The Assassin has advantage on attacks while Hidden.

Smoke Canister Action Fill the area within Close range of the Assassin with smoke. Each target in it has disadvantage on their next action roll. The Assassin can then become Hidden.

VariantAdded feature

Chapter 12

Ship Adversaries

Ship Adversaries

Enemy starships use the SRD's adversary stat blocks, so you run them like any other adversary: spotlight them with Fear, roll their d20 attacks against a ship's Evasion, and mark their Hit Points by damage threshold. Like all adversaries, their damage is a fixed roll, not multiplied by Proficiency.

Each ship lists its class after its role: Fighter, Freighter, or Capital. The class is also its scale, which raises or lowers the severity of damage between ships of different sizes. The full rules for crews, stations, maneuvers, and chases are in Starships and Space Combat.

TIE Fighter Flight

Tier 1 Minion (Fighter)

Cheap, fast fighters that win by numbers.

Motives & Tactics: Swarm, screen capital ships, close in

Difficulty: 11 | Thresholds: None | HP: 1 | Stress: 1

ATK: +0 | Laser Cannons: Close | 2 phy

Minion (4) Passive The TIE is defeated when it takes any damage. For every 4 damage a PC deals to the TIE, defeat an additional Minion within range the attack would succeed against.

Group Attack Action Spend a Fear to choose a target and spotlight all TIE Fighter Flights within Close range of them. Those Minions move within Very Close range of the target and make one shared attack roll. On a success, they deal 2 physical damage each. Combine this damage.

Source: Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope; Star Wars Rebels

Launch Bay Action Spend a Fear to bring two TIE Fighter Flights into the scene at Far range.

Tractor Beam Action Mark a Stress. A ship within Far range must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll (17) or become Restrained.

Broadside Action Spend a Fear to make a standard attack against every ship within Far range.

Momentum Reaction When the Star Destroyer makes a successful attack against a PC's ship, you gain a Fear.

Source: Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope; Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back

Broadside Action Spend a Fear to make a standard attack against every enemy ship within Far range.

Momentum Reaction When the Dreadnought makes a successful attack against a PC's ship, you gain a Fear.

Fleet Coordination Action When you spotlight the Frigate, mark a Stress to also spotlight two allied ships within Far range.

Droid Control Signal Passive If the battleship is a droid control ship, destroying it shuts down every Separatist droid adversary in the system at once.

Launch Vultures Action Spend a Fear to bring three Vulture Droid Flights into the scene at Far range.

Hangar Weak Point Passive A ship inside the battleship's hangar ignores the scale penalty against it, and its attacks against the reactor deal Severe damage on any success.

Diplomatic Flag Passive Attacking the cruiser openly has consequences: it carries envoys under Republic protection.

Salon Pod Reaction When the cruiser marks its last Hit Point, its salon pod detaches and flees at Very Far range with the envoys aboard.

A sturdy frigate that served the Republic as a medical and support ship, and later served the Rebellion the same way.

Motives & Tactics: Keep the fleet alive, shelter the wounded, retreat in good order

Difficulty: 13 | Thresholds: 14/28 | HP: 9 | Stress: 5

ATK: +1 | Turbolasers: Far | 2d8+3 phy

Medical Bays Action Mark a Stress. An allied ship within Close range clears 1 Hit Point.

Point Defense Reaction When an enemy fighter moves within Close range, mark a Stress to make a standard attack against it.

Acclamator-class Assault Ship

A Republic troop ship that can land on a planet's surface, carrying an entire battalion of clones and their gunships.

Motives & Tactics: Land the battalion, deploy gunships, hold the landing zone

ATK: +2 | Turbolasers: Far | 2d10+5 phy

Deploy Gunships Action Spend a Fear to bring two LAAT/i Gunships into the scene at Far range.

Planetary Landing Passive The assault ship can land and fight on a planet's surface, where it counts as a fortified position.

Source: Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones; Star Wars: The Clone Wars

Flight Deck Action Spend a Fear to bring two V-19 Torrent Flights or a V-wing Flight into the scene at Far range.

Broadside Action Spend a Fear to make a standard attack against every enemy ship within Far range.

Momentum Reaction When the Venator makes a successful attack against a PC's ship, you gain a Fear.

CR90 Corvette

Tier 2 Leader (Capital)

A Corellian corvette running blockades or escorting convoys.

Motives & Tactics: Control the lanes, escort convoys, run blockades, capture

Command Frequencies Reaction When a Minion within Far range is defeated, spend a Fear to bring another flight into the scene.

Hammerhead Corvette

Tier 2 Bruiser (Capital)

An old Sphyrna-class corvette with a heavy, blunt prow, famous among rebels for pushing a disabled Star Destroyer into another.

Motives & Tactics: Ram, shove, sacrifice for the mission

Ramming Prow Action Spend a Fear. The corvette rams a ship within Melee range, ignoring the scale penalty: the target takes 3d10+5 physical damage and is pushed to Close range. If the target is a disabled capital ship, the GM decides where it ends up.

Reinforced Bow Passive When the corvette would mark Hull from Minor damage, it marks a Stress instead.

Source: Rogue One: A Star Wars Story; Star Wars Rebels

Nebulon-B Escort Frigate

A long-necked escort frigate, built to guard convoys from starfighters, flown by the Rebellion and the New Republic.

Motives & Tactics: Screen the convoy, shoot down fighters, hold the line

Escort Screen Reaction When an allied ship within Close range is attacked, mark a Stress to give the attack disadvantage.

Fighter Complement Action Spend a Fear to bring two T-65B X-wings into the scene at Far range.

Source: Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back; Star Wars Rebels

MC80 Star Cruiser

A Mon Calamari star cruiser, organic in shape and layered with redundant shields: the heart of a Rebel or New Republic fleet.

Redundant Shields Passive Twice per scene, when the cruiser would mark Hull, reduce the severity by one threshold.

Fleet Command Action Spend 2 Fear to spotlight the cruiser and up to three allied ships within Very Far range.

Launch Fighters Action Spend a Fear to bring two T-65B X-wings or two RZ-1 A-wings into the scene at Far range.

Momentum Reaction When the cruiser makes a successful attack against a PC's ship, you gain a Fear.

Momentum Reaction When the battleship makes a successful attack against a PC's ship, you gain a Fear.

Chapter 13

Environments

Environments

Environments come in two kinds. Planetary environments are places on the ground: cantinas, checkpoints, forests, and ruins. Space environments are for scenes aboard starships, using the ship rules in Starships and Space Combat.

Planetary Environments

Locations your crew explores on foot or in vehicles, on the surface of a world or inside a station.

Wretched Hive Cantina

Tier 1 Social

A dim, crowded cantina where spacers, smugglers, and worse come to drink and deal.

Impulses: Offer work and trouble in equal measure, keep secrets, settle old scores

Difficulty: 10 | Potential Adversaries: Thugs, bounty hunters, smugglers, a cantina bouncer

What's the Word? Passive A PC can ask the bartender or patrons about local news, rumors, and work with a Presence Roll. On a success, they choose two of the details below, or three on a critical success. On a failure, they choose one and mark a Stress.

  • A rumor connected to a PC's background

  • A job involving a nearby threat or opportunity

  • A ship or pilot for hire

  • A warning about who else is in town

Who knows what? What do the regulars start saying about the PCs?

High-Stakes Sabacc Passive A PC can join a game of sabacc with a Presence or Instinct Roll. On a success, they win 1d4 handfuls of credits (2d4 on a critical success). On a failure, they lose a handful of credits or mark a Stress.

Who's at the table? Who's cheating, and who notices?

No Droids Passive The bartender refuses to serve droids. Droid PCs and companions have disadvantage on Presence Rolls with the staff.

Why does the bartender hate droids? Who agrees with him?

Hooded Stranger Action Reveal a stranger watching the PCs from a shadowed corner booth.

What do they want? How long have they been following the party?

Blasters Drawn Action Spend a Fear to start a brawl or shootout. While it lasts, a PC who moves through the room must succeed on an Agility or Presence Roll or take 1d6+2 physical damage. A PC can trigger this feature by provoking the wrong patron.

Who fired first? What will it take to stop it before the authorities arrive?

Spaceport Docking Bay

Tier 1 Social

A busy landing bay where ships refuel, cargo changes hands, and officials take their cut.

Impulses: Move cargo, check papers, take a cut

Difficulty: 11 | Potential Adversaries: Dock officials, stormtroopers, dock workers, rival smugglers

Papers, Please Passive Arriving or departing with cargo means passing inspection: a Presence Roll to bribe or bluff, or a Finesse Roll to present forged documents. On a failure, choose one: the officials find something they shouldn't, the crew pays a fine of 1d4 handfuls of credits, or the ship is held until the next day.

What's hidden in the cargo hold? Who on the dock is paying attention?

Parts and Labor Passive During a rest here, the crew can use the Patch Up and Overhaul downtime moves without a Tool Kit, and drydock repair prices apply.

Who runs the repair shop? What do they charge for asking no questions?

Someone's Watching the Ship Action Reveal a droid or stranger scanning the ship's registry.

Who sent them? What happens if the PCs confront them?

Lockdown Action Spend a Fear to lock down the spaceport. A tractor field holds every ship in its bay. Start a consequence countdown (4); at 0, troopers begin searching every bay.

What triggered the lockdown? Who else is desperate to leave?

Dune Sea Crossing

Tier 1 Traversal

An endless desert under burning suns, where water is life and the sand hides old wrecks.

Impulses: Bake, bury, wear down the unprepared

Difficulty: 11 | Potential Adversaries: Sand People raiders, scavengers, desert beasts

Merciless Suns Passive For each long stretch of travel without shade or water, each PC must succeed on a Strength or Instinct Roll or mark a Stress.

What landmark do they steer by? Who's running low on water?

Shifting Dunes Passive Navigating the dunes requires an Instinct or Knowledge Roll. On a failure, the party loses its way and the journey takes much longer.

What familiar shape on the horizon turns out to be wrong?

Wreck in the Sand Passive A PC who searches a half-buried wreck with a successful Instinct or Knowledge Roll finds salvage: roll on the Loot table at Common rarity.

What ship was this? What else is sheltering inside?

Raiders on the Ridge Action Reveal Sand People watching the party from a ridge at Far range.

What do they want? What sign tells the PCs they've been spotted?

Sandstorm Action Spend a Fear. Ranged attacks beyond Close range have disadvantage, and each PC caught in the open must succeed on an Agility or Strength Reaction Roll or take 1d6+2 physical damage.

Where can the party take shelter? What does the storm uncover when it passes?

Imperial Checkpoint

Tier 1 Event

A barricade of troopers and scanners standing between the PCs and where they need to go.

Impulses: Control, intimidate, catch the wanted

Difficulty: 11 | Potential Adversaries: Stormtroopers, scout troopers, an Imperial officer, a probe droid

Scan and Search Passive Passing through requires a Presence Roll to bluff or show credentials, or a Finesse Roll to use forged ones. On a success with Fear, a PC is pulled aside for a second inspection.

What are the troopers looking for today? What do the PCs have that they shouldn't?

Crowded Queue Passive PCs have advantage on rolls to blend into the crowd, but any violence here injures bystanders.

Who in line needs help? Who would report the PCs for a reward?

Wanted Bulletin Reaction When a PC with a known bounty or record approaches, you can spend a Fear to have the officer recognize them.

What crime is on the bulletin? Is the picture even accurate?

Raise the Alarm Action Spend a Fear. Start a consequence countdown (3); at 0, a squad of reinforcements arrives from Far range.

Where do the reinforcements come from? Where can the PCs run?

Forest Moon Canopy

Tier 1 Exploration

A forest of colossal trees, where villages hide in the branches and every shadow might be watching.

Impulses: Hide the hunters, protect the village, swallow the unwary

Difficulty: 11 | Potential Adversaries: Tribal warriors, scout troopers on speeder bikes, forest predators

Towering Trees Passive Climbing the trees requires an Agility Roll. A creature in the high branches can become Hidden.

What lives in the upper canopy?

Watchful Eyes Passive A PC who succeeds on an Instinct Roll notices small figures watching from the undergrowth.

Are they curious or hostile? What do they want from the PCs?

Snare Trap Action A PC triggers a hidden trap. They must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or be Restrained, dangling from a net in the branches.

Who set the trap, and how soon will they come to check it?

Speeder Patrol Action Reveal scout troopers on speeder bikes racing through the trees at Far range.

Are they hunting the PCs, or someone else?

Village in the Trees Passive If the PCs approach peacefully, a PC can make a Presence Roll to win a welcome. On a success, the villagers offer a safe place for a long rest and a guide through the forest.

What gift or story wins the village over? What do they ask in return?

Imperial Garrison

Tier 2 Exploration

A fortified base of gray corridors, security checkpoints, and troopers on constant patrol.

Impulses: Patrol, lock down, report everything

Difficulty: 14 | Potential Adversaries: Stormtroopers, Imperial officers, security droids, an AT-ST

Patrol Routes Passive Moving through the garrison unseen requires an Agility or Finesse Roll. On a failure, a patrol notices something is wrong.

Where do the patrols cross? Who's slacking off on duty?

Security Terminals Passive A PC can slice a terminal with a Knowledge Roll. On a success, choose one, or two on a critical success: open a sealed door, loop the security cameras, or download the base's layout and personnel files.

What else is on the terminal that the PCs weren't looking for?

Blast Doors Action Slam a blast door shut, splitting the party or cutting off their exit.

Who's on the other side? How long until it can be forced open?

Automated Turrets Action Spend a Fear. Each PC in an open area must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or take 2d8+3 physical damage.

Where's the control panel? Can the turrets be turned against the troopers?

Lockdown Protocol Action Spend a Fear. Start a consequence countdown (4). Each time it advances, a squad of troopers enters the scene. At 0, every exit seals.

What escape route hasn't been sealed yet?

Speeder Chase

Tier 2 Event

A breakneck pursuit on speeder bikes or landspeeders through forest, canyon, or city traffic.

Impulses: Close the gap, cut them off, punish hesitation

Difficulty: 14 | Potential Adversaries: Scout troopers on speeder bikes, swoop gangers, bounty hunters

The Chase Is On Passive Start linked countdowns: Escape (progress, 6) and Caught (consequence, 4). Rolls to drive, dodge, or fight back advance both.

Where are the PCs trying to reach? What happens if they're caught?

Narrow Gap Passive A PC who threads a tight opening with an Agility Roll made with disadvantage advances the Escape countdown by 2 more on a success.

What lies on the other side? Who's crazy enough to follow?

Run Them Off the Road Passive A PC within Very Close range of a pursuer can make a Strength or Agility Roll to ram them. On a success, the pursuer crashes out of the chase.

What do they crash into? Do they get back up?

Obstacle Field Action Each driver must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or take 2d6+3 physical damage.

What did they hit? Is the vehicle still running?

More Riders Action Spend a Fear to bring more pursuers into the chase at Far range.

Who called them? Are they faster than the PCs?

Undercity Depths

Tier 2 Exploration

The lower levels of a city-planet, where sunlight never reaches and anything can be bought.

Impulses: Hide the desperate, prey on the lost, keep the upper levels ignorant

Difficulty: 14 | Potential Adversaries: Gang members, cyborg enforcers, scavenger droids, undercity beasts

Endless Levels Passive Finding a specific place requires an Instinct or Knowledge Roll. On a failure, the PCs get lost, and the GM makes a move.

What landmark do locals use to find their way?

Black Market Passive Almost anything is for sale down here, including illegal goods, at double the usual price.

Who runs the market? What does it cost to buy their silence?

Gang Territory Reaction When the PCs cross into marked territory, you can spend a Fear to have the local gang demand a toll or attack.

What symbol marks their turf? What would earn their respect?

Falling Debris Action Each PC beneath falling debris must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or take 2d8+2 physical damage.

What fell, and was it an accident?

Frozen Battlefield

Tier 2 Event

An ice world's trenches and shield generators, with enemy walkers advancing through the snow.

Impulses: Freeze, entrench, overwhelm

Difficulty: 14 | Potential Adversaries: Snowtroopers, probe droids, ice beasts, Imperial walkers

Bitter Cold Passive Each scene a PC spends outside without cold-weather gear, they must succeed on a Strength Roll or mark a Stress.

Who brought the wrong coat?

Trench Line Passive Attacks against a creature in the trenches from beyond Close range have disadvantage.

Where does the trench line break?

Walkers Advance Action Spend a Fear. Start a consequence countdown (5); at 0, the walkers reach the shield generator and destroy it.

What can stop a walker? Who has the cables, the explosives, or the nerve?

Artillery Strike Action Spend a Fear. Each creature within Very Close range of a point within Far range must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or take 2d10+2 physical damage.

Who's buried in the snow?

Inside a Star Destroyer

Tier 3 Exploration

A warship the size of a city, with miles of corridors, thousands of crew, and hangars full of fighters.

Impulses: Swallow intruders, mobilize thousands, crush resistance

Difficulty: 17 | Potential Adversaries: Stormtroopers, death troopers, Imperial officers, mouse droids, an Inquisitor

Miles of Corridors Passive Finding a destination without a map requires a Knowledge Roll. On a failure, the PCs end up on the wrong deck, facing a patrol.

What does the stolen map get wrong?

Borrowed Uniforms Passive PCs in stolen uniforms have advantage on Presence Rolls to avoid scrutiny, until they do something no crew member would.

Whose uniform is it?

Tractor Beam Controls Passive A PC who reaches the remote terminal can disable the tractor beam with a Finesse or Knowledge Roll, freeing every ship in the hangar.

How exposed is the terminal? How long until someone notices?

Trash Compactor Action Trap the PCs in a compactor as its walls begin to close. Start a consequence countdown (3); at 0, each PC still inside takes 3d10+1 physical damage.

How do they get the walls to stop? What else is in the water?

Full Alert Action Spend a Fear. Start a consequence countdown (4); at 0, every hangar seals and a squad of death troopers arrives.

What route is still open?

Sith Temple Ruins

Tier 3 Exploration

An ancient temple of black stone, built on a wellspring of the dark side and full of old traps and older secrets.

Impulses: Whisper, tempt, guard forbidden knowledge

Difficulty: 17 | Potential Adversaries: Sith cultists, temple guardians, dark side beasts, an Inquisitor

Dark Side Nexus Passive Force Adepts have advantage on Spellcast Rolls here, but when they roll with Fear, they mark an additional Stress.

What does the power feel like? Who is tempted to stay?

Sealed Doors Passive Opening a sealed door requires a Knowledge Roll; on a failure, it triggers a trap.

What's carved on the door?

Whispers in the Dark Action A voice offers a PC what they want most. They must succeed on an Instinct or Presence Reaction Roll or mark a Stress as a vision overwhelms them.

What does the voice offer? What does the vision show?

Collapsing Halls Action Spend a Fear. Each PC in the area must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or take 3d8+3 physical damage.

What's revealed in the rubble?

The Relic Passive At the heart of the temple waits a Sith relic, such as a holocron or a wayfinder. Taking it is easy. Leaving the temple with it is not.

What does the relic want? Who else is searching for it?

Senate Chamber

Tier 3 Social

The great chamber of galactic government, where a single vote can save or doom a world.

Impulses: Delay, maneuver, play to the holocams

Difficulty: 17 | Potential Adversaries: Rival senators, Senate Guards, aides, a hidden assassin

Floor Debate Passive Swaying the chamber uses linked countdowns: Win the Vote (progress, 6) and The Vote Fails (consequence, 4). Presence and Knowledge Rolls during the debate advance both.

What's being voted on? Who controls the swing votes?

Backroom Deals Passive Outside the chamber, a PC can make a Presence Roll to strike a deal. On a success, they gain advantage on one roll during the debate, and a favor is now owed.

What's the price of that support?

Procedural Delay Action A rival senator calls for a committee review, stalling the vote while the opposition regroups.

Who benefits from the delay?

Assassin in the Gallery Action Spend a Fear to reveal an assassin taking aim from the gallery.

Who's the target? Who hired them?

Holocams Everywhere Passive Anything dramatic here is broadcast across the galaxy. A PC's public reputation shifts with what they do.

Who's watching the broadcast?

Superweapon Core

Tier 4 Event

The heart of a planet-killing battle station, humming with enough power to end a world.

Impulses: Charge, fire, end worlds

Difficulty: 20 | Potential Adversaries: Elite troopers, Imperial officers, turret batteries, a Sith Lord

Firing Sequence Passive When the PCs arrive, start a consequence countdown (8). It advances whenever a PC fails a roll or rolls with Fear. At 0, the weapon fires.

What's the target? Who will die if it fires?

Structural Weakness Passive A PC who succeeds on a Knowledge Roll finds the station's weak point. Start a progress countdown (5); successful attacks against the weak point advance it. At 0, the core begins to collapse.

How long will the PCs have to escape?

Reactor Shaft Passive A creature knocked toward the edge of the shaft must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or fall.

What's at the bottom?

Power Surge Action Spend a Fear. Each creature within Close range of the core must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or take 4d8+3 physical damage.

What does the surge knock offline?

Volcanic Duel

Tier 4 Event

A world of fire and collapsing platforms, where old friends become enemies and every step could be the last.

Impulses: Burn, divide, test resolve

Difficulty: 20 | Potential Adversaries: A Sith Lord, a fallen Jedi, magma-adapted beasts, mining droids

Rivers of Fire Passive A creature that ends its movement at the edge of the lava marks a Stress. A creature that falls in must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or take 4d10+10 physical damage.

How close is the edge?

Heat Shimmer Passive Ranged attacks beyond Close range have disadvantage.

What's hidden in the haze?

High Ground Passive A creature on higher ground has advantage on attack rolls against a creature below it.

Who reaches the high ground first?

Collapsing Platforms Action Spend a Fear. Each creature on a breaking platform must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or be carried to a point within Far range and mark a Stress.

Where does the platform drift? Who's left on it?

Final Words Reaction When a duel here reaches its end, with a PC or major adversary marking their last Hit Point, both sides can speak one last time before the outcome is decided.

What's left unsaid between them? Can they still turn back?

Space Environments

Space environments are for scenes aboard starships: dogfights, chases, jumps, and fleet battles. They use the same stat blocks and tier benchmarks as planetary environments, and their features target ships and crews under the rules in Starships and Space Combat. When a feature deals damage to a ship, compare it to the ship’s thresholds and mark Hull.

Asteroid Field

Tier 1 Traversal

A tumbling belt of rock and debris.

Impulses: Punish the reckless, hide the clever, collide

Difficulty: 11 | Potential Adversaries: TIE Interceptors, pirate raiders

Tumbling Rocks Passive A ship that moves farther than Very Close range through the field must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or mark a Stress.

Cover Passive A ship that flies close to the larger rocks can become Hidden.

Collision Course Action Spend a Fear to send a massive asteroid tumbling through the fight. Each ship within Close range of it must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or take 1d8+3 physical damage.

Ion Storm

Tier 1 Exploration

A crackling nebula full of static and charged particles.

Impulses: Blind, scramble, hide

Difficulty: 11 | Potential Adversaries: TIE Interceptors, smugglers

Static Interference Passive Attacks made from Far range or beyond have disadvantage.

Ion Surge Action Spend a Fear. Each ship must succeed on a Knowledge Reaction Roll or mark a Stress.

Trench Run

Tier 2 Event

A narrow canyon along the surface of a massive battle station.

Impulses: Funnel, punish, race the clock

Difficulty: 14 | Potential Adversaries: TIE Interceptors, turret batteries

Narrow Channel Passive Ships in the trench can only be within Melee or Very Close range of each other.

Run the Gauntlet Passive Start a progress countdown (6). Successful maneuvers and attacks advance it. At 0, the run is complete and the target is in sight.

Turret Batteries Action Spend a Fear. Each ship in the trench must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or take 2d6+3 physical damage.

Pursuit Reaction Start a consequence countdown (4) when the run begins. It advances each time the GM gains a Fear. At 0, a fast pursuer arrives behind the PCs.

Boarding Corridor

Tier 1 Event

A cramped docking tube or ship corridor.

Impulses: Choke, ambush, breach

Difficulty: 11 | Potential Adversaries: Stormtroopers, boarding droids

Cramped Passive Ranged attacks can't target anything beyond Close range.

Hull Breach Action Spend a Fear. A section decompresses: each character within Close range of the breach must succeed on a Strength Reaction Roll or be pulled toward it and mark a Stress.

Fleet Battle

Tier 3 Event

Capital ships trade broadsides across a battlefield of burning hulls while fighters swarm between them, as at Scarif and Atollon.

Impulses: Crossfire, overwhelm, swallow small ships

Difficulty: 17 | Potential Adversaries: Star Destroyers, Interdictors, TIE fighters, TIE Interceptors, TIE Advanced aces

Crossfire Passive A ship that moves between two capital ships within Far range of each other must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or take 3d8+3 physical damage.

Target the Flagship Passive Start a progress countdown (8). Attacks and missions against the enemy flagship's bridge, shield generators, or engines advance it. At 0, the flagship is crippled; all enemy Minions retreat and the rest of the fleet falls into disarray.

What's the flagship's weak point? Who has to get close enough to hit it?

Fighter Screen Action Spend a Fear to bring two TIE Fighter Flights into the scene within Close range of a PC's ship.

Capital Ship Breaks Apart Action A stricken capital ship, enemy or allied, breaks apart. Each ship within Close range of it must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or take 3d10+1 physical damage.

Whose ship was it? Who's still aboard?

Out of Hyperspace Action Spend 2 Fear to bring a Star Destroyer or an Interdictor into the scene at Very Far range.

The Akkadese Maelstrom

Tier 3 Traversal

A storm of gas and carbonbergs around Kessel, hiding a gravity well that swallows ships whole. Only the reckless try to cut through it.

Impulses: Crush, disorient, swallow

Difficulty: 17 | Potential Adversaries: Imperial blockade ships, pirates, a summa-verminoth

The Run Passive Crossing the Maelstrom uses linked countdowns: Through the Storm (progress, 6) and The Maw (consequence, 4). Pilot and Navigator rolls advance both.

Who said they could make it in record time? What's chasing them in?

Carbonberg Field Passive A ship that moves farther than Very Close range must succeed on a pilot's Agility Roll or mark a Hull.

The Maw Passive When The Maw countdown reaches 0, the ship is caught by the gravity well and its pilot must choose a ship death move.

Summa-Verminoth Action Spend a Fear. A colossal tentacled creature seizes a ship, which is Restrained and takes 3d10+1 physical damage each time the GM spotlights an adversary. It breaks free if the crew deals Severe damage to the creature or the pilot succeeds on an Agility Roll (17).

Raw Coaxium Reaction Once per scene, a ship carrying unrefined coaxium can pour it into the hyperdrive. The Engineer makes a Knowledge Roll (17). On a success, the ship jumps clear of the Maelstrom at once. On a failure, it marks 3 Stress.

What did the coaxium cost, and who wanted it?

Planetary Shield Gate

Tier 3 Event

A planet sealed beneath an energy shield, with a single orbital gate controlling everything that enters or leaves, like the Shield Gate above Scarif.

Impulses: Seal, trap, crush attackers between the shield and the fleet

Difficulty: 17 | Potential Adversaries: Star Destroyers, TIE fighters, TIE Interceptors

Planetary Shield Passive Ships and transmissions can't pass through the shield except through the gate while it's open.

Clearance Codes Passive A ship can request passage with stolen codes and a Presence Roll (17). On a success with Fear, the gate lets them through but logs the codes as suspicious.

Gate Closing Passive When the alarm sounds, start a consequence countdown (4). At 0, the gate seals. Anyone still below is trapped, and anything inside the gate when it closes is destroyed.

Bring It Down Passive The gate station has Difficulty 17, thresholds 22/40, and 6 Hull. Destroying it, or ramming a disabled capital ship into it, brings the whole shield down.

Who's still on the surface? Can they get a message out before the gate closes?

Gate Defenses Action Spend a Fear. Each ship within Close range of the gate must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or take 3d8+3 physical damage.

Superweapon Assault

Tier 4 Event

A desperate attack on a battle station that can destroy planets, like the battles of Yavin and Endor.

Impulses: Annihilate, recharge, spring the trap

Difficulty: 20 | Potential Adversaries: TIE Interceptors, TIE Defenders, Star Destroyers, an Executor-class Star Dreadnought

Superlaser Recharging Passive Start a consequence countdown (6) that advances each time the GM spotlights an adversary. At 0, the superlaser fires, destroying an allied capital ship or its target world, and the countdown resets.

Station Shield Passive While the station's shield is up, ships can't reach the surface. A ground team must bring down the shield generator first.

Who's on the ground team, and how much time do they need?

Surface Turrets Passive When a ship moves within Close range of the station's surface, it must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or take 4d8+3 physical damage.

Into the Superstructure Passive Reaching the reactor or exhaust port uses a progress countdown (6), advanced by successful maneuvers and attacks. At 0, one PC can make the final shot: an attack roll (20). On a success, the station begins to explode.

The Trap Springs Action Spend 2 Fear. An Imperial fleet, led by an Executor-class Star Dreadnought, arrives at Far range.

How long can the fleet hold on? Who will stay behind so others can make the run?

The Unknown Regions

Tier 4 Traversal

The galaxy's chaotic, uncharted edge, where hyperspace routes twist and few who enter ever return.

Impulses: Disorient, isolate, reveal what's hidden

Difficulty: 20 | Potential Adversaries: Hidden Imperial outposts, unknown ships, ancient guardians

Chaotic Hyperlanes Passive Plotting a course here uses Difficulty 20, and each jump advances a progress countdown (5) toward the destination. On a failure, the ship misjumps into a hazard of the GM's choice.

Far from Help Passive The crew can't buy supplies, fuel, or repairs. Each long rest, the ship marks a Stress unless the crew spends a handful of credits' worth of supplies.

Purrgil Migration Action A pod of purrgil, the great creatures that travel through hyperspace, appears. Each ship within Far range must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or be swept to a random point and mark a Stress. A Navigator who follows them with an Instinct Roll (20) advances the progress countdown by 2.

Where are the purrgil going? Do they know something the crew doesn't?

Something Watches Action Spend a Fear. A hidden outpost or an unknown ship scans the party. In The Dark Times, the party gains 1 Imperial Heat.

Who knows the party is out here now?

Chapter 14

Campaign Frames

Campaign Frames

A campaign frame provides inspiration, tools, and mechanics to support a particular type of story at the table. Each Kyberheart campaign frame covers one era of Star Wars canon and follows the Daggerheart SRD's format: a pitch, tone and themes, an overview, guidance for heritage and classes, player and GM principles, distinctions, an inciting incident, campaign mechanics, and session zero questions. Its complexity rating shows how much its mechanics add to the core rules.

The Dark Times

The Republic has fallen, the Jedi are hunted, and the Empire's grip tightens on every world. In the shadows, the first sparks of rebellion begin to catch.

Era: From Order 66 (19 BBY) to the Battle of Endor (4 ABY)

Complexity Rating: ●● (2)

The Pitch

Read this section to your players to introduce them to the campaign.

The Clone Wars are over, and the Republic is gone. In its place stands the Galactic Empire: a regime of order, fear, and endless white-armored troopers. The Jedi have been betrayed and hunted nearly to extinction. Worlds that resist are made examples of. Most people keep their heads down and hope the Empire never notices them. In a Dark Times campaign, you'll play the people who can't keep their heads down any longer: fugitive Jedi, deserting soldiers, smugglers with a conscience, and spies with nothing left to lose. You'll survive under the Empire's boot, fight for each other, and discover whether one small spark of defiance can become something the Empire can't stamp out.

Tone & Feel

Desperate, Gritty, Heroic, Hopeful, Paranoid, Swashbuckling, Tense

Themes

  • Hope in the Dark: What keeps you fighting when winning seems impossible?

  • The Cost of Resistance: What are you willing to sacrifice, and who pays the price when you act?

  • Complicity and Defiance: Is keeping your head down a choice? Where is your line?

  • Hidden Identities: Who are you when you can't be who you were?

  • Found Family: Who do you trust when anyone could be an informant?

  • Ends and Means: How far can you go to fight the Empire before you become what you're fighting?

Touchstones

All touchstones are official Star Wars canon.

  • Films: Revenge of the Sith (ending), Solo, Rogue One, A New Hope, The Empire Strikes Back, Return of the Jedi

  • Series: Andor, Star Wars Rebels, The Bad Batch, Obi-Wan Kenobi, Tales of the Empire

  • Games: Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order, Star Wars Jedi: Survivor, Star Wars Outlaws

  • Novels: Tarkin, Lords of the Sith, Thrawn, Catalyst, Ahsoka

  • Comics: Marvel's Darth Vader and Star Wars series, Doctor Aphra, Bounty Hunters

Overview

If your group decides to play this campaign, give your players the following information before character creation.

At the end of the Clone Wars, Chancellor Palpatine issued Order 66. Clone troopers turned on their Jedi generals, the Jedi Temple burned, and Palpatine declared himself Emperor of a new Galactic Empire. The Senate cheered. Over the following years, the clones were replaced by conscripted stormtroopers, and the Empire's reach spread to every sector.

The Empire rules through fear and paperwork. Moffs and governors command the sectors. The Imperial Security Bureau watches everyone, and informants are everywhere. Taxes, garrisons, and checkpoints squeeze the Mid and Outer Rim, while Imperial mining operations strip whole worlds. Nonhumans face open prejudice. Worlds that resist, from Ryloth to Kashyyyk to Ghorman, are crushed as an example to the rest.

The Jedi are gone, or so the Empire claims. A handful of survivors hide in the Outer Rim, hunted by the Empire's Inquisitors, dark side warriors with spinning red blades. Anyone who can feel the Force learns to hide it. A secret network, the Path, smuggles Force-sensitives to safety.

The galaxy's underworld thrives in the Empire's shadow. The Hutts, the Pyke Syndicate, Crimson Dawn, and Black Sun trade in spice, weapons, and people, and the Bounty Hunters' Guild has never had so much work. A good smuggler can make a fortune, as long as they don't ask what's in the crate.

Not everyone accepts the Empire. Across the galaxy, small rebel cells sabotage and steal, mostly on their own. Some are extremists, some are idealists, and some are criminals who found a cause. As the years pass, they begin to find each other. By the end of this era, they will be the Alliance to Restore the Republic, and they will face the Empire's ultimate weapon.

Your story happens in the margins of these great events. You may cross paths with famous heroes and villains, but the fight you're in is your own.

Choosing Your Starting Point

The Dark Times span more than twenty years. Choose when your campaign begins.

PeriodYearsWhat's happeningCanon touchstones
The Purge19–15 BBYOrder 66 and the Jedi Purge. Clones are decommissioned; the Empire consolidates.Revenge of the Sith, The Bad Batch, Tales of the Empire, Catalyst
The Dark Times14–6 BBYJedi survivors in hiding. The underworld flourishes. Resistance is scattered and isolated.Jedi: Fallen Order, Jedi: Survivor, Solo, Obi-Wan Kenobi
Sparks of Rebellion5–1 BBYRebel cells grow bolder and begin to unite into the Alliance.Andor, Star Wars Rebels
The Galactic Civil War0 BBY–4 ABYOpen war: Scarif, Yavin, Hoth, Bespin, and Endor.Rogue One, the original trilogy, Star Wars Outlaws

Communities

All communities are available, but some have unique aspects in the Dark Times.

CommunityIn the Dark Times
Jedi OrderThe Order is destroyed, so every Jedi-raised character is a fugitive. Were you a youngling, a Padawan, or a member of the Service Corps when Order 66 came? In later years, you may have been raised in secret by a survivor or brought to safety by the Path.
Sith AcolytesThe Inquisitorius takes Force-sensitives and breaks them into hunters. You might be a former Inquisitor trainee, an escaped captive, or raised among dark side cultists the Empire tolerates for its own reasons.
Imperial AcademyYou might be a defector, a deserter, a rebel agent wearing the uniform, or a loyal officer starting to doubt. Decide in session zero whether loyal Imperial characters fit your table.
BatchThe clones were decommissioned and replaced by stormtroopers. A clone PC either had their inhibitor chip removed or it never worked, and they're a deserter wanted by the Empire.
Mandalorian CovertThe Empire's Great Purge of Mandalore scattered the clans. Coverts hide in the Outer Rim, while some Mandalorians serve the Empire as Imperial Super Commandos.
Rebel CellBefore the Alliance forms, most cells work alone and distrust each other. Some, like Saw Gerrera's Partisans, are willing to do anything to win.
SyndicateThe Hutts, the Pyke Syndicate, Crimson Dawn, and Black Sun all thrive in the Empire's shadow, and all of them make deals with it.
City-WorldCoruscant is now Imperial Center, the heart of the Empire, where the upper levels gleam and the lower levels hide everything else.
Orbital ShipyardsKuat's yards build Star Destroyers for the Empire, while Mon Calamari shipwrights will one day build the Rebellion's great cruisers.
Canopy ClansKashyyyk is occupied, and many Wookiees have been enslaved. Endor's forest moon remains unknown to most of the galaxy.

Ancestries

All ancestries are available. The Empire openly favors humans, and nonhuman characters face suspicion, harassment, and worse from Imperial officials. Consider how this shapes your character's life.

  • Droids wear restraining bolts and get regular memory wipes. A droid PC with their own will might be a former Imperial droid who was reprogrammed, or one whose owner never wiped them.

  • Wookiees were enslaved after the Empire occupied Kashyyyk. A Wookiee PC may be an escaped slave or a fighter in the resistance.

  • Twi'leks from Ryloth live under Imperial occupation, and Cham Syndulla's freedom fighters still resist.

  • Chiss are rarely seen in known space, though one, Thrawn, rises to become an Imperial Grand Admiral.

Classes

All classes are available, but some have unique aspects in the Dark Times.

  • Force Adepts must hide what they are. A lightsaber seen by the wrong person is a death sentence, and using the Force near Imperials draws Imperial Heat (see Campaign Mechanics). A Sith PC might be an Inquisitor who escaped, or a dark side user the Empire wants obedient or dead.

  • Operatives and Consulars thrive in an era of spies and politics. Until the Emperor dissolves the Senate in 0 BBY, rebel sympathizers still serve in it, gathering secrets and support.

  • Soldiers might be clone deserters, former stormtroopers, or rebel commandos.

  • Bounty Hunters find that Imperial bounties on rebels and Jedi pay very well. Will your character take them?

  • Scoundrels and Pilots run blockades, smuggle for the syndicates, and fly for the Rebellion.

  • Technicians slice Imperial systems, repair aging ships, and keep droids out of Imperial hands.

Player Principles

If your group decides to play this campaign, give your players the following information before character creation.

Make the Empire Personal. The Empire has taken something from your character: a home, a family, a name, or a future. Let that loss shape what they want and what they're willing to risk.

Hope Is an Action. In the Dark Times, hope isn't a feeling; it's something you do. Look for small acts of defiance, kindness, and courage, even when they seem hopeless.

Trust Is Earned. Anyone could be an informant. Let your character be wary, but let the crew earn each other's trust over time. That trust is worth more than any blaster.

Live in the Margins. The galaxy's great battles happen with or without you. Your story is in the shadows of those events, and that's where heroes are made.

GM Principles

Keep the following guidance in mind while you GM this campaign.

Make the Empire Vast, Banal, and Human. The Empire isn't just Darth Vader. It's a bored checkpoint officer, an ambitious ISB supervisor, a frightened eighteen-year-old in white armor, and a regulation that ruins a family. Show the machine and the people inside it.

Canon Is the Backdrop. Major canon events happen on schedule unless your table agrees otherwise. The Death Star is built, Alderaan is destroyed, and the Rebellion wins at Endor. Let the PCs shape the margins of those events, as the heroes of Rogue One and Andor do.

Let Every Act Cost Something. Defiance brings consequences: reprisals on civilians, rising Imperial Heat, lost allies, and hard choices. Make victories feel earned.

Light Small Sparks. Show that small victories matter: a freed village, a stolen shipment, a broadcast that reaches the right person. Hope should grow over the campaign.

Keep the Legends Offstage. Canon heroes and villains appear rarely and never take the spotlight from the PCs. When Darth Vader arrives, treat him as a storm to survive, not a fight to win.

Distinctions

This is where GM-facing information begins. Share what you like with your players, but these are the pillars and secrets you'll build your story on.

The Galactic Empire

Emperor Palpatine rules from Imperial Center, with Darth Vader as his enforcer. The galaxy is divided into sectors governed by Moffs, and Grand Moff Tarkin's doctrine holds that fear of force keeps worlds in line better than force itself. The Imperial Security Bureau hunts dissent, and Imperial Intelligence watches everything else. The Imperial Senate survives as a hollow formality until the Emperor dissolves it in 0 BBY. Most Imperials aren't monsters. They're careerists, conscripts, and true believers who think they're keeping the peace, which makes the Empire far more dangerous.

The Jedi Purge and the Inquisitorius

After Order 66, the Grand Inquisitor and his Inquisitors hunt surviving Jedi and Force-sensitive children from the Fortress Inquisitorius on Nur. A few Jedi survive in hiding, and a secret network called the Path smuggles Force-sensitives to safety. A Jedi who reveals themself brings Inquisitors within days.

The End of the Clones

The clone army is decommissioned and replaced by conscripted stormtroopers, and Kamino's cloning facilities are destroyed. Some clones desert. A few, like Captain Rex and Clone Force 99, fight back. Secret: deep in the Empire, research into cloning and Force-sensitive blood continues at Mount Tantiss.

The Empire's Secret Projects

Secret: Kyber crystals are disappearing from Jedha and other holy sites. They're bound for Project Stardust, the Death Star, under Director Krennic and the reluctant scientist Galen Erso. The station destroys Jedha City and Alderaan before it falls at Yavin, and a second Death Star rises above Endor.

The Growing Rebellion

Resistance begins as scattered cells. Luthen Rael's secret network funds and arms them, quietly bankrolled by Senator Mon Mothma, while Bail Organa supports the growing rebellion through his own channels. Saw Gerrera's Partisans fight on Jedha with brutal methods. An agent called Fulcrum feeds intelligence to cells like Phoenix Squadron. After atrocities like the Ghorman Massacre, the cells unite into the Alliance to Restore the Republic, which establishes its base on Yavin 4.

The Underworld

Jabba the Hutt rules Tatooine's underworld. The Pyke Syndicate runs the spice mines of Kessel. Crimson Dawn, led by Qi'ra after Dryden Vos's fall, works from the shadows. Black Sun and smaller gangs like the Haxion Brood fill the gaps, and the Bounty Hunters' Guild takes Imperial contracts without asking questions. Every syndicate makes deals with the Empire, and every one would betray it for the right price.
